News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Sports.title: Huddersfield Giants to leave home for Dewsbury amid major investment
Sports.content:
Betfred Super League side Huddersfield Giants have announced they are to leave the town and move to Dewsbury for the 2027 season onwards.

The Giants' intention is to move into Dewsbury's Flair Stadium, subject to RFL board approval, investing a projected £10m-plus in developing the ground.

The investment will deliver a transformational upgrade of the venue, including the construction of a new stand that will increase capacity from 5,000 to around 8,000 spectators, creating a viewing area on all four sides of the pitch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Huddersfield Giants director of rugby Andy Kelly reflects on what he's described as the 'most challenging' period of time in charge of the club

The redevelopment will also feature refurbishment of the fan concourses, significant upgrades to existing and new hospitality suites, new bars and food areas, both male and female player dressing rooms, and press facilities elevating the stadium to Super League standards.

An agreement has been reached following extensive and amicable negotiations with Betfred Championship team, Dewsbury Rams, and a strong partnership between the two clubs has been forged. The Flair will continue to host the Rams in the newly-upgraded and dual-branded facility.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Huddersfield Giants prop Tom Burgess joins Jenna, Jon and Sam Tomkins on The Bench

This comes following a period of uncertainty for the Giants after seeking a permanent location in the Huddersfield area.

Owner of the club, Ken Davy OBE, has explored several alternative sites, including The Shay Stadium in Halifax.

Speaking of the decision, Davy said: "It's no secret that as a club, we have fought to find a home in Huddersfield. We had to move from Fartown, from Leeds Road, and now from the Accu Stadium. But the Huddersfield Giants will not retreat. We will not compromise or quietly shuffle into the shadows.

"While we remain the Huddersfield Giants, I am proud to announce that our stage for the 2027 season and beyond is Dewsbury.

"The Flair Stadium is the perfect location for us, it will have the right capacity and facilities for the Giants and its fans to thrive while we continue the search for our permanent home. Our one giant future starts now.

"My overriding aim is to create a purpose-built stadium within Huddersfield for the Giants to call home. My commitment on that has not wavered. However, that was not feasible for the 2027 season."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Huddersfield Giants against Hull FC from the Super League

Ralph Rimmer OBE, executive chairman of the Huddersfield Giants, added: "The Giants' future is bright, and we are excited to lead the club into this new era.

"For fans, the matchday experience will be our focus. A smaller, more intimate ground means the crowd is closer to the action, letting the atmosphere grow and support the team out on the pitch.

"The Flair Stadium offers everything that supporters need from parking and accessibility to corporate hospitality and function rooms.

"We can't wait to welcome you for the 2027 season and beyond to be a part of the Giant future we have in store."

Jackson: Dewsbury not yet Super Lsague ready

Huddersfield Giants non-executive director Rebecca Jackson:

"[Dewsbury flair stadium] is not quite Super League ready yet, so we definitely need to bring it up to standard.

"We'll be spending around £10m - a huge investment - to ensure that it can actually be the place where the Huddersfield Giants can play, and really have the atmosphere for both the fans and our partners - and that means building a new stand too, which is very exciting.

"This is just a medium-term plan. We are still looking to build our own stadium within Huddersfield, which has been something that we've worked on for a really long time.

"We've just unfortunately not been able to secure a site quite yet with the local authorities, but a lot of discussion has been happening.

"We're hoping that this is going to be able to be a bit of a stop gap for us - a medium-term solution - to then be able to get back into Huddersfield long term."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Moore helps GB and Ireland to Shergar Cup crown
Sports.content:
Ryan Moore bagged a Shergar Cup double on his return to the competition following a 20-year absence to help his Great Britain and Ireland team win the team event while he was also crowned leading rider over the six races.

Winner of the Silver Saddle on his last appearance at the team-based meeting in 2006, Moore has usually been required to ride on a Group One card in Ireland.

But with that meeting put back 24 hours he was free to attend and delighted the Ascot crowd.

Team Great Britain and Ireland topped the standings on 81 points from Team Hong Kong in second on 62, with Moore's individual haul of 47 enough to take the Silver Saddle.

He first struck on Dylan Cunha's Asgard's Captain (13-2) who stuck to his task gamely to win the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge by a length and a quarter from Yutake Take on Sportingsilvermine for the Rest of the World.

Moore said: "Dylan did say he could be a little bit lazy, but he has an uncomplicated attitude and to just help him through it and it was straightforward, really.

"It's great to get Dylan a winner here today and the owners will be delighted as they were all looking forward to it, so it's a good job the horse has performed today."

In the penultimate Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic, he gave Marco Botti's Archers Bay (5-2) a textbook ride coming home three-and-a-quarter lengths clear of Christophe Lemaire on King Of Berkshire for Team Europe.

Having run in the Italian Derby earlier in the season, he looked the class act and so it proved.

In the closing Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile, Moore finished third on Ozat behind the Frida Valle Skar-ridden Crown Board (10-1), but her Team Europe were not in contention for top honours by then.

Saffie Osborne thrives in the team environment and got her name on the scoresheet when Tim Easterby's Red Spells Danger justified 2-1 favouritism in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint.

Osborne was leading rider in the Racing League on three occasions and is captaining Moore and Dylan Browne McMonagle in Team Great Britain and Ireland.

She said: "I heard a few people knocking this horse today but I thought the track would really suit and it has. I'm just glad I pulled my finger out.

"Looking at the standard of jockeys here today, it's amazing - look at our team with Ryan Moore and Ireland's champion jockey.

"The win for me today is that I made Ryan laugh a couple of times, so I'm quite happy with that!"

Team Hong Kong had earlier set the pace winning the first two races.

Jerry Chau gave them the perfect start when partnering Tuco Salamanca to a clear-cut victory in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash.

Representing a team making its Shergar Cup debut, Chau, 26, gave Ollie Sangster's four-year-old the perfect ride, taking a lead into the final furlong before a gap opened up seamlessly.

Tuco Salamanca (4-1) quickened impressively to beat Gold Star Hero, ridden by Chau's team-mate Vincent Ho, by a length and a half.

Fandom and Suraj Narredu were third for the Rest of the World.

Chau told Sky Sports Racing: "It felt amazing when I hit the line.

"No words can describe riding a winner at Ascot. I grew up watching Ryan Moore on YouTube. I watched him as much as I could."

Luke Ferraris did not have to wait long to play his part for Team Hong Kong as after an opening race one-two from his team-mates, he drove home Dancing In Paris to win the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers.

Riding the Ian Williams-trained 17-2 shot, Ferraris came with a late run to collar Moore on Andrew Balding's Shrimp Shady to win by a length.

Mountain Road was third for Yutake Take and the Rest of the World.

Ferraris said: "That's phenomenal, he's a lot fitter than me! He was turned out in great order.

"He didn't settle as good as he should have, but he still produced a great turn of foot.

"I think I've only ridden in one two-mile race in recent years, so it was a bit of a change.

"We've a good group of young riders representing Hong Kong, so let's hope it continues."

Sports.title: Nicholls pays tribute as Big Buck's dies aged 23
Sports.content:
Big Buck’s, one of the greatest staying hurdlers of all time, has died at the age of 23.

Owned by the late Andy Stewart, he was part of a golden age for trainer Paul Nicholls as he counted Kauto Star, Denman, Master Minded and Neptune Collonges among his stablemates.

Big Buck's had always been viewed by connections as a potential top-class chaser, however, a fall at the final fence in the 2008 Hennessy Gold Cup saw him revert back to hurdles and he never looked back.

He won what is now the Stayers' Hurdle a record four times, the Liverpool Hurdle four times and three times he came home in front in the Long Walk Hurdle.

Big Buck's, who struck up a great relationship with Ruby Walsh, was a fan favourite as he would often hit a flat spot in his races before powering to victory.

Nicholls told the Press Association: "Ability-wise he was probably as good as anything I've ever trained, it's just a shame he couldn't jump a chase fence.

"He was a wonderful horse for a wonderful owner who deserved to own a great horse like that. Andy enjoyed the whole journey and shared it with everybody.

"The horse had a brilliant life and had a great time with us and then a great time with Mike and Lucy Felton in retirement, but sadly time caught up with him.

"I was very lucky to have him at the same time as Kauto Star, Neptune Collonges, Master Minded and Denman. He was definitely as good as any of them."

Image: Big Buck's and Ruby Walsh formed a formidable partnership

One of the last surviving members of that halcyon period for the Ditcheat handler, Big Buck's would go on to pass Sir Ken and win a then record 18 straight National Hunt races when reverting to hurdles, an achievement only eclipsed by Altior since.

However, for Nicholls there will always be the question of how high he could have climbed if remaining over the larger obstacles.

"He won the Graded race at Aintree over fences, jumped 18 fences and jumped them 18 different ways and still won," said Nicholls.

"It made me think he was a certainty in the Hennessy and he was unlucky that day, but he just wasn't a natural jumper of a fence.

"If Kauto Star hadn't been about at that time then we probably would persevered over fences and he had the ability to win a Gold Cup. If he had won the Hennessy that day it would have definitely given us a headache and it would have been interesting where he would have ended up.

"But over hurdles he was invincible. Andy said I was bonkers, but going back over hurdles was the best thing we ever did. History tells you how good he was and Cheltenham, Aintree, Newbury, Ascot - if there was a big staying hurdle race, he won them all - all those Grade Ones on the trot, what a horse."

Big Bucks would become a standing dish on Thursdays at the Cheltenham Festival, with his famous flat spot often sparking nervous gasps from supporters before hitting top gear and surging up the Cheltenham hill under Walsh.

When asked to nominate just one race in Big Bucks' decorated career littered with so many great triumphs it was his fourth-straight success in the day three feature, when seeing off arguably the deepest field he met, edging out Irish raider Voler La Vedette, that Nicholls remembers most fondly.

"His fourth World Hurdle was the one that sticks out as being very special," said Nicholls.

"But we had so many great days with such a brilliant horse and we were all very lucky to be associated with him."

Sports.title: Australia survive late Japan rally as new coach Kiss makes winning start
Sports.content:
Australia held on for a tight 35-32 victory over Japan, despite a first-half red card for Miles Amatosero, as they made a winning start in head coach Les Kiss' first match in charge.

The Wallabies were forced to dig deep, battling the heat as well as being a man down, holding off a strong comeback from Japan to emerge victorious.

"That was tough, wasn't it? Not just the conditions," said Kiss. "They're a good team. They ​play fast and hard at home in their backyard.

"Probably offered a few too many opportunities for them. We'll have a look at it. But overall, that's a Test win. Well done, boys."

Image: Les Kiss was previously head coach of Queensland Reds

Kiss took over from Joe Schmidt as head coach last month after Australia finished the first phase of the Nations Championship with one win in three - a victory over Italy following on from losses to Ireland and France .

For Australia's two-Test series against Japan, Kiss included only one uncapped player, centre Isaac Henry, but recalled big, versatile Reds forward Lukhan Salakaia-Loto and left out veteran James Slipper.

The Wallabies were forced to scramble after Amatosero was red-carded in the 32nd minute for a dangerous clean-out on Warner Dearns. Initially shown a yellow card, it was upgraded to red just before the break, which the teams entered locked at 14-14.

Tries from Max Jorgensen and Fraser McReight early in the second half helped Australia build a nine-point lead but Japan steadily ate into that advantage with a pair of penalties from Takuro Matsunaga.

The quality of Australia's bench proved the difference as it allowed the visitors to keep up the pressure on Japan, and Taniela Tupou crashed over to give them a 10-point lead with 10 minutes remaining.

Japan captain Dearns set up a grandstand finish when he found a way over, reducing the lead to three, but Australia held on.

Image: Former Australia and England head coach Eddie Jones is in his second stint in charge of Japan

Eddie Jones, the former Australia and England head coach, is in his second stint in charge of Japan.

"We let ourselves down with a few fundamental ​errors in the last 20 minutes when we had an opportunity to probably put Australia away, so pretty disappointed, mate," said Jones.

"But yeah, I'm really proud of how hard the players ‌are playing and there's a lot of development ​in this team."

Sports.title: Sullivan attends West Ham game despite being advised not to
Sports.content:
David Sullivan stepped down as West Ham director in June after an investigation into sexual misconduct allegations; he strongly denies all allegations of wrongdoing; he attended Carabao Cup tie against Portsmouth despite being advised not to

West Ham: David Sullivan attends Carabao Cup first-round tie with Portsmouth despite being advised not to

Former West Ham United chairman David Sullivan attended the Carabao Cup first-round tie against Portsmouth at the London Stadium

David Sullivan attended West Ham's Carabao Cup match against Portsmouth at the London Stadium on Saturday, despite him being advised to stay away from home matches.

Sullivan resigned as a director and joint chairman of West Ham in June, before the publication of an investigation by The Times and BBC Panorama into sexual misconduct allegations. He has strongly denied all allegations of wrongdoing.

On Monday, a spokesperson for London Stadium told Sky Sports News it had "recommended" to West Ham that Sullivan does not attend matches because of concerns about fan unrest.

The West Ham United Fan Advisory Board (FAB) also called on Sullivan not to attend the club's home matches, warning his presence could become a "distraction" and a potential security concern.

In a statement, the FAB said it remained concerned that Sullivan attending matches at the London Stadium would cause "offence and upset" to some supporters and could provoke negative reactions from fans.

The FAB also pointed to West Ham's ground regulations, which state that entry can be refused to any individual whose presence could constitute a source of danger, nuisance or annoyance to others

West Ham beat Portsmouth 3-1 to progress to the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Sports.title: Joao Pedro nets double as Chelsea bounce back to beat Milan
Sports.content:
Chelsea bounced back from back-to-back pre-season defeats with their best performance under Xabi Alonso so far as Joao Pedro's double helped them to a convincing 3-0 win over AC Milan in Jakarta.

The Blues' previous hybrid between 4-2-3-1 and Alonso's patented 3-4-3 was ditched in favour of the latter and paid off against the Serie A heavyweights, with Marco Palestra shining at left wing-back and the impact of new set-piece coach Austin McPhee already evident.

Chelsea scored 10 goals from corners across the whole Premier League season in 2025/26 but managed two in 90 minutes here, with Joao Pedro peeling off Milan goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani to glance Moises Caicedo's delivery home unmarked, moments before the break.

He doubled his and Chelsea's lead within a minute of the restart by pouncing at the back post to turn home Pedro Neto's in-swinging cross, before Caicedo turned provider to scorer by latching onto a volley from another corner from the edge of the box three minutes later.

Chelsea could have had more with substitutes Geovany Quenda and Nicolas Jackson both lively and denied by the woodwork, but they could settle for a morale-boosting victory and more than an hour in the legs for most of a strong starting line-up in Indonesia.

Image: Joao Pedro nodded Chelsea ahead moments before half-time

The key moments from Jakarta...

Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged ‘lover’
Sports.content:
Uefa has confirmed a “departure payment” was made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Gianni Infantino while he was the organisation’s general secretary, allegations Fifa has dismissed as “categorically untrue”.

The Daily Telegraph reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum following the alleged relationship with Infantino. In a statement, Uefa confirmed a payment was made along with covering the fees for an MBA course, which it said was “in line” with regulations at the time.

However, Fifa has responded to the reports. “Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory,” a Fifa spokesman told the Telegraph. “No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.”

The report comes as pressure mounts on Infantino following his plan to seek private investment in a company which would run Fifa’s competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups. Infantino worked at Uefa for 16 years and was its general secretary from 2009 before being elected as Fifa president in February 2016.

A Uefa spokesperson said: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for a MBA course at a local business school.”

The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time. “Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all Uefa employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.”

Infantino has found himself at the centre of a storm for two weeks following his controversial plan to sell stakes to private investors in a company to run the World Cup. The plan was rejected by Uefa and two other continental confederations. On Wednesday, Infantino was backed by Fifa’s management board following a meeting in Morocco and issued an apology over the process.

Uefa’s threat for its 55 member countries to boycott Fifa competitions until the plan was scrapped remains, with the European confederation saying on Thursday that Wednesday’s announcement “changes nothing”.

Sports.title: West Ham sink Pompey in Carabao Cup as Sullivan ignores advice to stay away
Sports.content:
In an unseasonable black bomber jacket, with heavy duty company beside him, David Sullivan took his seat. Against the advice of the stadium’s operators, unbowed by serious allegations placed against his name and the weight of public opinion, West Ham’s major shareholder, the former co-chair, sat with arms crossed, always conspicuous by his presence.

By beating Portsmouth in relative comfort, 3-1, West Ham, the club where Sullivan’s name is no longer above the door, had secured a heartening Carabao Cup passage to the second round. There, they will be reunited with their former Premier League peers. The serious Championship business begins next Sunday at Burnley. Whether Sullivan travels north for that remains to be seen. It cannot be ruled out.

Before kick-off, the London Stadium big screen showed a “countdown to walkout”, referring to the players’ arrival rather than to fans deserting the scene in protest. This being West Ham in 2026, any confusion would be understandable. Taking previous mutinies into account, and despite a summer of intrigue and anger, there were surprisingly few audible or visible signs of insurrection as season 2026-27 began, and an extended 90 minutes was played out.

Even with Sullivan’s arrival expected, the gate to the directors’ car park did not stage a welcoming committee, the lanes around the London Stadium quiet. Protests there have been a regular sight, targeting Sullivan and his departed associate Karren Brady.

Even once Sullivan’s presence was confirmed there was nothing resembling the barracking of last season. Instead, the loudest boos of the first half came at a hydration break at its midway point, with an odd choice of 90s rave musical accompaniment. The legacy of a North American World Cup continues to darken.

Perhaps still-searing temperatures and a dose of early optimism had doused the fires raging when the Hammers’ drop was confirmed in May. Time-served Irons know plenty about relegation; their club has dropped down each decade since the 1970s; West Ham heritage.

The kick-off chorus of I’m Forever Blowing Bubbles drowned out the Pompey Chimes ringing out from 9,000 away fans. As is usual for away fans at the London Stadium, the visiting contingent decried their surroundings and the Faustian pact struck for West Ham’s tenancy.

Football has rarely been in focus during West Ham’s summer of tumult, boardroom battles after Sullivan’s defenestration. So what of football? Carabao Cup Saturday served as a decent dry run for their attempt at a promotion campaign.

View image in fullscreen David Sullivan takes his seat at the London Stadium just after kick-off. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images

The new West Ham closely resembled the former West Ham though shorn of the £151m worth of player sales that took in Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts. Joël Veltman, the sole summer signing so far, on the bench, came on with three minutes left.

In midfield, Edson Álvarez, who spent last season on loan to Fenerbahce, lined up alongside Lewis Orford, a 20-year-old it is hoped can follow the path of Frank Lampard, Michael Carrick and Mark Noble, the latter a mentor, into becoming a first-team regular.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The torpor of a first 30 minutes of little footballing consequence was broken by a Portsmouth goal, scored by Adrian Segecic, via a deflection off Maximilian Kilman, an expensive purchase far too regularly on the crime scene.

It took 10 minutes for West Ham to awaken before Mohamadou Kanté’s pirouetting feint laid up Taty Castellanos to equalise. Mere moments later, Jarrod Bowen, the club captain staying on to lead his club back up, a rare adult in the room last season, lashed in their second.

Both goals evidenced a quality that ought to guide the club back to the Premier League with some comfort, though nothing should be taken for granted.

For the record, Sullivan kept any celebrations to himself and returned for a second half that began with Castellanos nodding in Bowen’s cross. An afternoon that might have descended into a familiar seething pit of rage and resentment now offered grounds for optimism. Though just beyond the hour, a chorus of “stand up if you hate the board”.

If Sullivan is no longer a board member he was its undoubted target. He has turned many a deaf ear down the years, and continues to do so.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup: Preston prevail in Goodison home game, Millwall keeper saves four penalties
Sports.content:
Delano Burgzorg scored the winning penalty in the shootout after Jusef Erabi equalised in stoppage time for 10-man Preston to knock Huddersfield out of the Carabao Cup. The game took place at Goodison Park, the former Everton men’s ground, due to Preston’s Deepdale pitch not being ready.

Daniel Iversen saved two penalties, after a thrilling end to normal time that ended 1-1 when Erabi cancelled out Radinio Balker’s strike. Preston played 69 minutes without Lewis Gibson who was shown a red card.

Set-pieces proved dangerous for Huddersfield and with seven minutes left in the first half, Balker scored with a header. Preston struggled with the man disadvantage in the first half, but after the break they applied more pressure and in the third minute of added time Erabi drilled the ‘home side’ level.

Burgzorg ended the shootout with a clinical penalty after Huddersfield missed two and Andrew Moran had his spot-kick saved by Matty Young.

Millwall’s goalkeeper, Lukas Jensen saved all four QPR spot-kicks as the visitors won 2-0 on penalties at Loftus Road. A late own goal by Mark Sykes cancelled out Luke Cundle’s second-half opener in a 1-1 draw after 90 minutes. Jensen superbly kept out efforts from Ilias Chair, Harvey Vale and Koki Saito before his save from Kwame Poku sealed the victory.

View image in fullscreen Lukas Jensen of Millwall is mobbed by teammates at Loftus Road. Photograph: Andrew Fosker/Shutterstock

Cambridge mounted a speedy comeback to beat Barnet 2-1. The visitors went ahead soon after half-time, but the Us hit back through Ben Knight and Isaac Heath to lead only eight minutes later.

Barnet took the lead four minutes after half-time. Callum Perry and Kell Watts made outstanding blocks on the line, but their efforts proved in vain as Kabongo Tshimanga tucked the rebound away.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimarães completes £75m Arsenal move: ‘I needed a new challenge’
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimarães says he “needed a new challenge in my life” after joining Arsenal from Newcastle for £75m and has targeted winning trophies. Guimarães is understood to have signed a four-year contract that contains a further one-year option after Newcastle reluctantly agreed to sell their captain.

The 29-year-old, who captained Newcastle to their first trophy since 1955 when they won the Carabao Cup last year, had made it clear that he wanted to join the Premier League champions after meeting the club’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, this week.

Arsenal have previously shown an interest in signing Guimarães on two occasions – in 2020 when he was playing for Athletico Paranaense in Brazil and then 18 months later when he was at Lyon and went on to move to the north-east. But the Brazil midfielder said he wanted to join Arsenal after his first meeting with Mikel Arerta and the sporting director, Andrea Berta.

“I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life,” he told Arsenal’s website. “After playing two World Cups, I’m at the point of my life, I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I’m in the right place to do it.

“I’m so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season, so the squad is going to be very, very important and I’m hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

The arrival of Guimarães significantly boosts the midfield options available to Arteta, who now has a formidable squad that contains Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

“We are further strengthening the heart of our team,” said Berta. “As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity and has provided goals and assists for his team every year. Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.”

Guimarães revealed he has already received a message from Rice welcoming him to Arsenal that said “come here and please no more fights, now we’re friends”. “I was happy he messaged me, but the midfield we have here, is one of the best in Europe,” said Guimarães. “Everyone is an amazing player. I’m so excited to start chatting and play, and know the players very, very well,”

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães said leaving Tyneside was ‘one of the toughest decisions of my life’. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

Guimarães also released a statement to Newcastle. He said: “I fell in love with this place. I really mean that. From my first day, the supporters, my teammates, Eddie [Howe] and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home.

“This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together. I thank PIF, our chair, Yasir Al-Rumayyan, and Jamie Reuben for everything they have done for me and for this football club. I also want to say thank you to David [Hopkinson, the Newcastle CEO] and Ross [Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director] for the huge respect to me throughout this process. They did everything they could to keep me at Newcastle, and I am very grateful for our time together.”

On Friday, Wilson said they had no option but to allow Guimarães to leave. “What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, he effectively told us he wanted to leave,” he said.

“That doesn’t mean he can go, but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. There’s no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer – it wasn’t. But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen.”

Sports.title: Jorge Messi, father and agent of Argentina great, dies aged 68
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi’s father and agent, Jorge, has died aged 68 at a medical clinic in the ⁠Argentinian city of ⁠Rosario after ​a long illness, the family have announced. Jorge Messi spent his final months ⁠alternating between a medical centre in Rosario and his home, accompanied by his wife, Celia, and his ⁠children Rodrigo, Matías and María Sol.

Lionel Messi ​spent time with his ‌father after the World ‌Cup before rejoining his club, Inter Miami, for whom he ‌returned to action a week ago. Inter Miami are due to play Monterrey on Saturday at home in the 2026 Leagues Cup, but the MLS club have yet to announce whether he will feature.

Newell’s Old Boys announced the death in a social media post that said he had undergone treatment in recent months for an unspecified illness. The post described him as “the pillar and the person who, with vision, rigour and affection, supported the career of the best player of all time, alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini”. The Argentinian FA also expressed its ⁠condolences in a statement, saying: “From here, we stand in solidarity ​with the entire family ​during this difficult time and send ​the most heartfelt, warm, and affectionate embrace. Strength to you all.”

View image in fullscreen Lionel Messi poses with his brother Rodrigo, sister María Sol, father Jorge, mother Celia, nephew Tomás and brother Matías in Rosario, Argentina, in 2003. Photograph: El Grafico/Getty Images

At the World Cup, Lionel Messi said after Argentina’s 3-0 victory over Algeria – when he broke down in ​tears while celebrating ​his first goal in the team’s opening match – that he was going through a difficult personal situation. Later, he explained his tears ​were due ‌to “something unrelated to ​football” after ​going through “a few difficult, complicated days”.

There was speculation that the player’s emotional reaction to Argentina’s last-16 victory over Egypt was due in part to his father’s deteriorating condition. A few days later, the family issued a statement regarding Jorge Messi’s “health situation”, informing the public that he was undergoing medical treatment.

Jorge Messi closely accompanied his son throughout his career, beginning with his early years at Barcelona. He acted as a crucial pillar of support and, for several years, served as his representative. “I always ‌needed my dad’s approval, ever since I was a kid. After every match, I’d ask him ​what he thought of how I played,” said Lionel Messi.

Sports.title: Liverpool agree to sign Barcelona’s Ronald Araújo on loan as Jacquet cover
Sports.content:
Liverpool have agreed to sign Ronald Araújo on a season-long loan from Barcelona after Andoni Iraola was faced with lack of defensive options for the start of the new season.

Concerns over Jérémy Jacquet – the France Under -21 defender who arrived last season for more than £50m – and injuries to Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni have left Liverpool short of options at the back after the departure of Ibrahima Konaté on a free transfer to Real Madrid.

Araújo, who was part of the Barça side that won La Liga last season, will add much-needed cover in the short-term. The Uruguay defender is expected to complete his medical on Sunday.

The deal for the 27-year-old is believed to contain an option to buy at the end of the season. Araújo has made more than 200 appearances for Barcelona, but only made 11 league starts last season.

Liverpool have shown an interest in Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa, but were put off by the £60m valuation of the England defender. Arsenal have had an initial approach for Konsa rejected.

Jacquet, who signed from Rennes in February, has not made a competitive appearance after picking up a serious shoulder injury last season and did not feature during Liverpool’s three-match tour of the United States. Iraola said last week that he has been feeling “some discomfort, so we don’t want to rush him”.

The Liverpool manager added: “He comes from a lot of months without playing. And obviously I would like to try with him with Virgil [van Dijk] when he recovers, because with the injury of Joe we’ve been without senior centre-backs. But we have to be careful with Jeremy.”

Sports.title: Why Super Furry Animals joined music’s dash to cross over football’s vinyl frontier | Emma John
Sports.content:
As someone born on the cusp of the gen X-millennial divide, I am the perfect target for today’s 90s nostalgia. I played my modest, teenage part in the Battle of Britpop (verbal skirmisher, Blur division); I fervently sang – and, God help me, believed – that Things Can Only Get Better. Super Furry Animals were a band I knew only distantly, via the transgressive thrill of that song they had with all the swearing in. And yet the news they’ll be shirt sponsor for a Welsh football club this season has managed to whisk me straight back to a time when things seemed simpler, kinder and more hopeful.

Nearly three decades have passed since Super Furry Animals last had their logo on a football kit. Back in 1999, their frontman Gruff Rhys and bassist Guto Pryce, both Cardiff City fans, persuaded their Bangor-born bandmates to lay down their north Wales allegiances for the duration of the Bluebirds’ Welsh Cup run – which was, incidentally, all they could afford. The cup shirts cost them £2,000 and were, according to Rhys, knock-offs made for ice hockey. This year’s beneficiaries are a more modest outfit: Cwmbran Celtic, just relegated from Wales’s second tier. Cwmbran is the town where the band send their stage props for repair, and given the props in question are giant inflatable bears, you wonder whether they could get one installed in goal.

Super Furry Animals aren’t the only 90s band involved: Scottish post-rockers Mogwai have sponsored the men’s away strip, with 10% of the profits from all shirt sales going to a grassroots music charity.

There has traditionally been an element of patronage when famous musicians do football, from Elton John’s time as chair of Watford, to Robbie Williams’s 2024 elevation to Port Vale club president. The pattern is a repeating one: local lads (they’re usually lads) make good, and want to give back to the team they’ve followed since they were little. Wet Wet Wet were the first to go down the shirt-sponsorship route with Clydebank in 1993. The team’s shirts turned out to be a more timeless design than the loud, oversized suits that Marti Pellow’s crew wore the day they unveiled them.

Slapping your logo on your home side’s shirt was a charitable endeavour, rather than an investment. Nothing underscored this point better than Fatboy Slim’s relationship with Brighton & Hove Albion. The DJ’s record label first sponsored their shirts in the late 90s, back when the team’s financial straits had left them flirting with extinction, and Tony Bloom’s billions were still waiting to be won. It was particularly appropriate back then that Micky Adams’s men should run out on to the field with their chests declaring them SKINT.

View image in fullscreen Bobby Zamora in Brighton’s home kit sponsored by Fatboy Slim. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

Musical match-ups have tended, therefore, towards the endearing, not the cool. Jake Bugg sponsored Notts County not to market his own music, but to evangelise the Midlands team on his global tours. And it’s even cuter when bands have sponsored kids’ teams. The late Lemmy of Motörhead was tickled by the thought of a Lincolnshire under-10s team sporting his Snaggletooth skull mascot on their fronts; unfortunately the resultant all-black kit too closely resembled referees’ uniforms and the children were banned from wearing it in league matches. Still, the idea had an enduring appeal: the Prodigy, Biffy Clyro, Sleaford Mods and Franz Ferdinand have all paid for youth kits.

In the last couple of years, though, the relationship between bands and football teams has turned serious. The move to monetise the “adjacent audiences” of pop and sporting fandom means shirt sponsorship is no longer a way of artists showing their support, but a marketing and merchandising opportunity in its own right.

Spotify’s deal with Barcelona got the ball rolling, with Coldplay, Karol G, Rosalía and Travis Scott each briefly appearing on the shirtfront, and limited-edition replicas costing more than £340 a pop. The footie-kit-as-streetwear trend means bands aren’t “sponsors” any more, they’re “collaborators”. Hence Manchester United’s pre-match shirts don’t bear the name of the Stone Roses, just their album artwork. And while that may have baffled a few younger fans – the club’s website ran a post explaining who the Madchester group were for the gen Z-ers – it still reflects a genuine connection. Ian Brown is a lifelong Red, and the team has walked out to This Is the One since Gary Neville first requested it two decades ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Coldplay show off their Barcelona shirts. Photograph: Fc Barcelona Handout/EPA

Whereas a year ago, if you’d been asked at a pub quiz what Paris Saint-Germain had in common with a K-pop band, or what Pink Floyd had to do with a Serie A team, you’d have been within your rights to say “nothing”. The answer, now, is clothing ranges – PSG teamed up with the girl group Blackpink to optimise fan engagement in Asia, while Inter marked the 50th anniversary of the album release of Wish You Were Here.

All this can be confusing for the simple-minded sports lover like me. What is a culture-forward lifestyle capsule, anyway? It sounds like something Musk and Bezos want to blast to Mars in. Creating a sporting look now involves an advanced understanding of fashion arithmetic: at last year’s Euros it was Admiral x Spice Girls, now it’s the Rolling Stones x England Cricket x Castore. These are powerful equations, as when a 2025 Bohemian FC x Fontaines DC shirt (raised to the power of Greta Thunberg when she wore it on her flotilla to Gaza) = £££££ for charity. Maybe Ed Sheeran’s Mathematics tour top for Ipswich was an omen. Or perhaps this is a fad, and the music industry will soon move on to something new. GQ, which has declared “blokecore” over, says we’ll be wearing classic rugby tops by autumn/winter. Sounds delightfully 90s to me.

Sports.title: Will Lankshear starts off in style to see Middlesbrough past Wrexham
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear’s debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round. Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener but when Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter’s cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle’s cross and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt. Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento’s cross into Lankshear’s path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining but Morgan Whittaker’s low strike rebounded off the post.

After the match the Middlesbrough manager, Kim Hellberg, expressed his delight with the instant impact Will Lankshear has made since joining the club. “He was very impressive and the most impressive thing has been seeing how well he has worked on the training ground,” Hellberg said. “How hard he works on the training ground and how much he wants to learn.

“It’s a joy to watch and when you add the person he is to the quality he has as a footballer on the pitch, you have a very good striker. I’m happy to have him here.”

Wrexham’s manager, Phil Parkinson, felt his side had given a decent account of themselves just four days after returning from a pre-season tour of the US. Parkinson said: “I thought we had enough half-chances, particularly in the first half, to have progressed in the competition. The game really separated from one quality finish from their lad. We had some good build-up play, but just didn’t quite have that clinical edge.

“It was a big ask in terms of coming back from America on Monday and you’ve got to give the lads credit for going close. There were a lot of positives in the performance.”

Sports.title: New EFL signing immediately forced to clarify ‘stepping stone’ comment amid backlash
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough signing Radek Vitek has been forced to explain a comment made during his first interview after his transfer.

Vitek signed for Boro from Manchester United on Friday, but he said that the move was a 'new stepping stone' for him.

2 New Middlesbrough goalkeeper Vitek received backlash for his first interview Credit: Getty

His wording led to some backlash from fans online, as they questioned his mentality regarding the switch.

Typically, the phrase 'a stepping stone' relates to a player using a smaller club solely as a route to join a bigger team in the future, rather than planning to stay for a long time.

After Middlesbrough posted a video of Vitek's first interview as their new signing on Saturday, supporters flooded the replies.

One Boro supporter replied on X: "Don’t love how he has just called us a stepping stone."

Another questioned: "Did he just say stepping stone..."

"Lad really said ‘new stepping stone’ Jesus. Welcome to the club, I guess," a third Boro fan posted.

But some fans jumped to Vitek's defence and pointed out a language barrier that could have impacted the Czech star.

"I think he means 'next step in my career' having listened to it a few times," another Middlesbrough supporter said. "Easy to mix up sayings when it's someone's second language."

'Not meant in any negative way'

And just a few hours after Vitek's first interview was posted and he faced some backlash, he spoke out on the matter.

"I wanted to clarify what I meant by 'stepping stone'," the goalkeeper wrote, explaining his words on his X account.

What did Radek Vitek say in his interview? In the video posted by Middlesbrough on Saturday, Vitek could be heard saying: "A new challenge for me. "A new stepping stone in my career, a permanent move. "So I'm really excited. I hope everyone is as excited as me for the season ahead and I hope we can go for the goal we all want."

"I just want to assure everyone that I have not meant that in any negative way.

"The point of this comment was that this is a very important step in my career going forward.

"I can’t wait to get started."

Off to a controversial start

Vitek won't have wanted any controversy to begin his time as a Middlesbrough player, but he has now cleared things up.

The 22-year-old has joined the club from Man United after spending the last six years with the Red Devils.

He spent last season on loan at Bristol City in the Championship, following other loans in the EFL and Austria.

2 Vitek spent pre-season with Man United after a loan at Bristol City last term Credit: Getty

Vitek was named Bristol City's Player of the Year after an impressive campaign - and now he's back in the second tier.

Away from his 'stepping stone' comments in his first interview as a Boro player, he also said: “It feels great to be here.

“This is a new challenge for me and I’m really excited to be a Boro player.

“The project here is very impressive, because you can clearly see the ambition and where the club wants to go.

“I’m delighted to now be part of that.”

Sports.title: South Korean FA apologises after headquarters raided over sexual services for refs allegations
Sports.content:
South Korean FA apologises after headquarters raided over sexual services for refs allegations

South Korea’s FA has issued an apology following reports that it had provided 'sexual services' to foreign referees.

The country’s broadcaster JTBC reported earlier this week that the Korea Football Association (KFA) had offered the services to officials that were in the country for international matches.

3 The South Korean FA is under the microscope yet again Credit: AFP

The allegations date back more than a decade ago with referees offered services on multiple occasions in 2011 and 2012.

It is alleged that further indiscretions occurred prior to qualifying matches for the 2014 World Cup and the 2012 London Olympics.

In a statement, the KFA profusely apologised for the details of the report.

KFA's statement on shock allegations

It read: “We deeply apologise for causing concern over various issues involving the association, which emerged from a parliamentary hearing and an unprecedented search and seizure, and from reports about events from more than a decade ago, that even many within the organisation were unaware of.'”

The news report published on Thursday revealed how a sports ministry investigation back in 2016 found the KFA had provided inappropriate entertainment to foreign referees.

It claimed that it happened on seven separate occasions between March 2011 and March 2012.

The services included trips to massage parlours with the fees inclusive of the costs of sexual services.

“The association makes clear that inappropriate conduct of this kind, or the use of corporate cards for such purposes, is absolutely not currently taking place,” the KFA added in its statement.

The allegations come after a period of instability on and off the pitch in South Korean football.

A review into an issue involving the appointment of former national team coach Hong Myung-bo is ongoing.

3 Hong Myung-bo's appointment as South Korea head coach is under investigation

Seoul police raided the KFA’s offices on Thursday as part of their inquiries into Hong’s selection.

The investigation began shortly after Hong’s appointment but to a halt this summer after nearly two years without answers.

However, public anger surrounding South Korea’s disappointing World Cup group-stage exit brought about renewed attention.

Ex-KFA technical director Lee Lim-saeng is accused of offering Hong the job at a bakery near the coach’s home.

South Korea’s sports ministry said in 2024 that Lee’s meeting with Hong was not a formal interview and that the KFA had breached its own hiring rules.

However, the ministry found no evidence of foul play.

3 South Korea endured a hugely disappointing World Cup campaign this summer Credit: AFP

“When I received the offer, I thought they had all taken the proper steps,” Hong said at the parliamentary hearing.

“People may think things were not so transparent, but I never once asked for any special treatment.”

Sports.title: Mason Mount sparks new injury fears by limping out of Man United pre-season game
Sports.content:
Mason Mount sparks new injury fears by limping out of Man United pre-season game

Mason Mount was forced off with an injury scare during Manchester United's pre-season clash with Paris Saint-Germain.

The 27-year-old has been blighted by fitness issues since his move to Old Trafford in 2023, but was named in Michael Carrick's starting XI as they took on the European champions in Gothenburg.



4 Mount was in conversation with Man United's medical team after lasting less than 20 minutes against PSG Credit: X: @samuelluckhurst

4 The Englishman headed straight down the tunnel after his afternoon was cut short Credit: X: @samuelluckhurst

But there was no let-up for Mount in the pre-season fixture, as he pulled up early on and was unable to continue.

The 27-year-old then had to be replaced by Tyler Fletcher in yet more concerning scenes.



After exiting the field, Mount could be seen deep in conversation with members of United’s medical staff.

He then made his way down the tunnel, in a familiar sight for Red Devils supporters.



Man United were 1-0 down to a youthful PSG side when Mount was forced off, with Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye putting the Champions League winners in front within two minutes.

But Carrick's side responded soon after, as Bryan Mbeumo equalised shortly after the half-hour mark.



In the wars

Injuries have plagued Mount's Man United career, preventing him from reaching the standards he set at previous club Chelsea.

The Cobham academy graduate joined the Red Devils in a £60million deal in 2023.

However, since then he has spent a staggering 394 days on the sidelines, causing him to miss both Euro 2024 and this summer's World Cup with England.

Mount has made just 72 appearances for United, but made his most appearances in a Premier League campaign for the club last term.



4 Mount was in Sweden for Man Utd’s latest pre-season clash Credit: Getty

The England midfielder featured 23 times in the league, scoring three goals, although he was mainly used by former boss Ruben Amorim in the first half of the season.

This has led to rumours he could join Amorim at new club AC Milan, although Mount has been part of United's pre-season group so far.

Make or break?

Mount's latest setback against PSG come after talkSPORT's Shebahn Aherne suggested that the upcoming season was make-or-break for him in his career.



“He needs to have a strong season,” Aherne said of Mount.

“Luke Shaw played every game last season and really got his season back on track, sorted out the injury issues and he was brilliant.

“But Mason Mount, you always hear that he’s the perfect pupil. He’s a very smart and intelligent player and when he’s on his game. He’s brilliant.

4 Mount has scored just seven goals in his injury-hit Man United career Credit: Getty

“You just hope that this season he will come good.”

talkSPORT's Tony Cascarino was also hopeful the 27-year-old could find his level again and highlighted one of his key attributes.



He said: “They paid £55m for him. He was injured at Chelsea before he got to Old Trafford and he was a terrific player for Chelsea.

“He can play in that floating position like [Florian] Wirtz and he can get a goal.

“Manchester United need a really fit Mason Mount, if not to start, then to challenge for other player’s spots in the team.

“He’s a good finisher, get him in goalscoring positions and he will finish. It would be like a new signing.”

Sports.title: Are hydration breaks now part of English football? Carabao Cup stoppages roundly booed
Sports.content:
If there was one thing that English football fans did not want to see introduced to the game this season, it was hydration breaks.

So, why did some fixtures in the Carabao Cup first round on Saturday see a pause in play called by the referee for a drink?



2 Hydration breaks caused plenty of fan backlash at the World Cup Credit: Getty

It appeared to take some supporters by shock as the largely condemned World Cup rule appeared to be used in England.

Halfway through each half in multiple ties across the country, including at West Ham's London Stadium and Leicester City's King Power, a break was called for the teams to take on some fluid.

And as those in the stands realised what was happening, a chorus of boos and angry chants filled stadiums - a reaction that is not surprising.



Hydration breaks were one of the main talking points of the summer, as every World Cup game was split into four quarters.

Each half of each game at the tournament saw a pause in play that allowed players to have a drink, but the break ended up becoming a chance for a team talk with the manager and coaches too.



FIFA were slammed for including the breaks, which were added to the rules to help out players when playing in scorching heat.

There were also many questions raised over whether that was the sole reason, or whether they were introduced for extra commercial time on TV coverage in the United States.



But with the World Cup over and temperatures not reaching the heights of those in the US during the 3pm kick-offs in the Carabao Cup, why were the hydration breaks used on Saturday?

Are hydration breaks now in English football?

Fortunately for fans in England, despite some expecting the breaks to eventually become the norm, it is not a new rule.

The EFL has told talkSPORT that it is not a new competition policy in the Carabao Cup to have the hydration pauses.

2 The EFL have not made hydration breaks a new competition policy Credit: Getty



There were breaks in the play during the first round clashes purely down to the decision of the officials in charge.

The referees decide on an individual basis depending on the weather, which is the standard protocol in the EFL - with temperatures on Saturday reaching highs of 29 degrees Celsius.

So, thankfully, it is not expected that the official hydration break ruling will be introduced in English football anytime soon.

Carabao Cup on talkSPORT

talkSPORT has you covered throughout the Carabao Cup first round this weekend - and can entertain you during the breaks!



You can follow live coverage of Colchester vs Southampton at 5:30pm on Saturday evening on talkSPORT 2.

And coverage of Mansfield vs Sheffield United follows on Sunday.

Then, next weekend, talkSPORT brings you live commentary of seven different games from the Championship's opening gameweek.

Sports.title: David Sullivan publicly defies London Stadium recomendation in West Ham opener
Sports.content:
David Sullivan has defied advice to stay away from the London Stadium by attending West Ham's Carabao Cup tie against Portsmouth.

The 77-year-old stepped down from his position as club chairman in June ahead of the release of a joint investigation by The Times and BBC Panorama accusing him of sexually-exploitative behaviour.



3 David Sullivan defied advice to keep away from the London Stadium in West Ham's first competitive game of the season Credit: Getty

Sullivan categorically denied the claims made against him in the investigation, which saw seven women come forward.

Despite stepping down from his role as chairman, the former adult industry kingpin remains West Ham's largest shareholder.

However, the London Stadium confirmed earlier this week that it had 'recommended' that Sullivan stay away from home fixtures this season.



This followed an internal investigation which deemed there was not an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with him attending matches.

The club asked for advance notice of any planned visits by Sullivan - who retains a 38.8 per cent stake in the Irons - in order to implement additional safety and operational measures.



Staying put

West Ham's Carabao Cup clash with Portsmouth on Saturday saw them kick off their first competitive game of the season.

And Sullivan appeared to ignore advice from the London Stadium, as he was spotted in the stands for the Hammers' 2026/27 opener in east London.



However, there did not appear to be any problems inside the stadium before and shortly after kick-off.

This marks the first competitive fixture the Hammers have played since the allegations against him were first reported.

It also saw the club begin their campaign following relegation from the Premier League to the Championship last season.

3 Sullivan appeared to go unnoticed by fans as he took his seat at the London Stadium Credit: Getty



As well as being advised to stay away from the London Stadium, the investigation into Sullivan also revealed he had been banned by the FA from having contact with West Ham’s women's and youth teams since 2023.

His suspension from doing so came after allegations and a safeguarding investigation, and meant he was unable to attend matches involving either side.

Changing landscape

Sullivan bought a 50 per cent stake in West Ham alongside David Gold 16 years ago and currently holds a 38.8 per cent share.

While he currently remains the club's largest single shareholder, a change in boardroom at the London Stadium looks increasingly likely.



There is an ongoing tussle for shares in the Hammers between a consortium led by Amanda Staveley and current second-largest shareholder Daniel Kretinsky.

The Czech billionaire is attempting to stop Staveley from purchasing the Gold family's 25.1 per cent stake in a £150million deal.

3 Jarrod Bowen marked the news that he will remain at West Ham this season with a goal against Portsmouth Credit: Getty

While West Ham continue to navigate a summer of upheaval on and off the pitch, they focused on the task in hand against Portsmouth.



After falling behind to Adrian Segecic's deflected effort in the first half, the east Londoners fought back to turn the game on its head.

After Taty Castellanos' equaliser, captain Jarrod Bowen then fired the Hammers in front on the stroke of half-time.

This was Bowen's first goal since penning a new deal to stay at the club for the upcoming season, and West Ham's lead was soon doubled as Castellanos grabbed another on 50 minutes.

West Ham will then begin their Championship campaign away to Burnley on Sunday, August 16.

Sports.title: Will Lankshear left clueless after falling victim to brand new EFL rule
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear left clueless after falling victim to brand new EFL rule

Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear became the first player to fall foul of the EFL’s new time-wasting rule.

The 21-year-old, who recently completed a permanent switch from Tottenham, later admitted he was unaware of the newly-implemented regulation.

2 Will Lankshear scored a sublime winner for Middlesbrough against Wrexham but endured a frustrating end to his night Credit: Getty

It was an eventful night for Lankshear who netted the only goal of the game in Boro’s 1-0 win over Wrexham in the Carabao Cup first round on Friday.

However, shortly afterwards he fell victim to a new rule designed to clamp down on time wasting during substitutions.

The new law states that if a player takes in excess of ten seconds to leave the pitch after his number has been shown, then his replacement will only be allowed to enter the field of play at the first stoppage after a minute has elapsed.

The rule was enforced at this summer’s World Cup and will also be applied in the Premier League this coming season.

Lankshear was replaced 20 minutes after his goalscoring heroics where he superbly netted an overhead kick winner.

But his 81st-minute exit, which included him applauding the home supporters at the Riverside Stadium, was deemed to have broken the rules.

That left his replacement Fin Cartwright waiting more than 60 seconds before being granted access to the pitch.

It briefly left Boro with a player down in their quest to reach the next round of the Carabao Cup.

Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg was seemingly aware of the rule and was seen urging his striker to quickly leave the pitch.

However, Lankshear later admitted he had no idea about the rule.

2 Lankshear was left bemused by the new ruling Credit: Getty

“I didn’t know,” Lankshear said.

“I haven’t been in the referee meetings at the start of the year because I came from Tottenham.

“I now know to get off the pitch a lot quicker!”

The deal to take Lankshear to Middlesbrough could end up costing the Championship club up to £20million.

He was among a host of recent exits from the north London club with Luka Vuskovic, Tynan Thompson, Alfie Devine and Alejo Veliz all having moved on.

Middlesbrough kick off their Championship campaign at home to Lincoln next weekend.

Sports.title: ‘The adventure continues’ – Andros Townsend joins 17th club of professional career
Sports.content:
Andros Townsend has signed for Thai top-flight side PT Prachuap, continuing his playing career in Asia aged 35.

The transfer brings Townsend to his 17th different club and sees him remain in Thailand after a move last summer.



2 Townsend has been announced as a new PT Prachuap player Credit: Instagram / @ptprachuapfc

The former Premier League winger signed for Kanchanaburi Power in a surprise move in August 2025, playing 30 games.

He scored three goals and provided six assists in his first term.

But the club were relegated from Thai League One, leading to him making another switch to stay in the top flight.

And now, Townsend has joined PT Prachuap, who finished sixth in the table when his former side finished at the bottom.



'The Thai adventure continues'

Announcing the arrival of the former England international, the club posted on social media: "Get ready. He’s here.

"Time to welcome the new members of the carnage army. See you on the field. Welcome to the Killerwasp Family."



And Townsend himself reacted to the post of him donning his new side's merchandise, sharing the images on his account.

Alongside a heart eyes emoji and the Thai flag, the veteran wrote: "The Thai adventure continues"



PT Prachuap were founded in 2009 and managed to achieve promotion to Thai League One nine years ago.

They will hope that the addition of the experienced ex-Premier League forward can bring them some more success.

2 Townsend is heading into a second year playing in the Thai top-flight Credit: Getty

Townsend's long career

Townsend, who has 13 England caps to his name, has now joined the 17th club of his long professional career.



He made his pro debut with Tottenham in 2009 and remained at the club for seven years, eventually leaving in 2016.

During his stint, he made eight different loan moves, featuring for Yeovil Town, Leyton Orient, MK Dons, Ipswich, Watford, Millwall, Leeds, Birmingham and QPR over a four-year spell.

A move to Newcastle came for Townsend in 2016, and he played for the Magpies for five years before joining Crystal Palace.

He also played for Everton, Luton and Turkish side Antalyaspor before making his move over to Thailand in 2025.



In total, Townsend has made 291 Premier League appearances, scoring 26 goals and providing 31 assists in the top-flight.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi suffers tragic loss of father as Jorge Messi dies aged 68
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's father, Jorge Messi, has passed away at the age of 68 after battling illness.

The father of the Argentine football icon had been experiencing health issues recently, which the Messi family confirmed during the World Cup.

3 Jorge was the father of Argentina superstar Lionel Messi Credit: Getty

Jorge was a central figure in Messi's career, having acted as his son's agent since the age of 14.

Tribute paid

Messi's first club, Newell's Old Boys, paid tribute in a statement.

It read: “Club Atlético Newell’s Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario.

“Recognized leproso fan, businessman, and father of the Argentine national team captain, Lionel Andrés Messi.

“Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini.

“His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory.

“Thank you for teaching him to love these colours.

“The Board of Directors, members, athletes, and the entire leprosa family embrace with affection Celia, Lionel, Rodrigo, Matías, and María Sol, and all their loved ones and close ones in this difficult moment.

“Farewell forever, leproso."

His death comes less than a month after it was revealed that Jorge had been 'under medical supervision' for an unspecified health issue.

3 Jorge Messi has passed away following a battle with illness Credit: Getty

With this occurring at the start of the World Cup, Messi was in tears after scoring his first goal of the tournament against Algeria, and later revealed he had been struggling with issues off the pitch.

Speaking post-match, he said: “My tears after the first goal? I’ve had some tough days, it wasn’t related to football, and those feelings were because of that.

"I thank my teammates, the technical staff, and the delegation for helping me.”

As well as acting as his agent, Jorge was the driving force behind Messi's career.

He travelled with his son to Barcelona when he first joined the Spanish giants' famousLa Masia academy as a 13-year-old.

Jorge remained at Messi's side throughout his unprecedented career, which has seen him win a staggering 13 Ballon d'Or awards, four Champions League titles, and the 2022 World Cup.

3 Jorge Messi was in the ground as his son won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar Credit: Getty

Messi's father was in attendance to watch him lift the Jules Rimet trophy in Qatar, a moment which many felt cemented his status as football's greatest-ever player.

Jorge is survived by his wife, Celia Maria, and sons Lionel, Rodrigo and Matias, and daughter Maria Sol.

Newell's Old Boys city rivals, Rosario Central, also paid tribute to Messi's father.

In a post on X, the Argentine club wrote: "El Club Atlético Rosario Central deeply regrets the passing of Jorge Messi.

"We accompany with respect and affection Lionel, his family, and all his loved ones in this painful moment. May he rest in peace."
