World.title: Why journalism is dying in Nigeria!, By Olayinka Oyegbile
World.content:
Today, every unemployed or unemployable journalist wants to carry a ‘dignified’ title of being a publisher, hence the rash of poorly edited and managed online publications in the cyberspace. It has become a case of ‘read one and you’ve read all’; no variety, no nuance, and no depth. News stories now read the same and flat! Features have become tasteless and investigation poor, if any.

All the metrics for legacy news media are headed in the same direction: less revenue, far fewer reporters and editors, less profit to reinvest and less community clout. – Rory O’Connor

It is not in doubt that journalism around the world is undergoing tremendous changes and threat: technology, dictatorship, problems of funding and self-inflicted wounds (knowingly or unknowingly) inflicted by journalists on the profession in recent times, are some of the threats confronting the profession.

Some of these problems are not new. They are age old and only present themselves in new formats. For instance, in the 1980s when Ray Ekpu was removed as editor of the high-flying Sunday Times, the paper whose sales figures he had moved up significantly, and was sent to the Business Times as editor. He was determined to recreate the magic that he performed at Sunday Times there. However, when the atmosphere became too toxic and he saw that he was not given the free hand needed to change the staid and dull nature of business reporting as editor, he had to move to the Concord Group at the invitation of his friend (the late) Dele Giwa. He was made chair of the Editorial Board there.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Concord became stronger and profited from the loss of the Daily Times Group. Later when his friend (Giwa) began to have issues with the publisher, the trio of Giwa, Ekpu and Yakubu Mohammed left the Concord Group and teamed up with Dan Agbese to found Newswatch. The magazine changed the face and phase of magazine journalism in Nigeria. The quartet didn’t quit to establish their own newspapers or magazines individually, they teamed up.

The same happened years later when Nosa Igiebor, Onome Osifo Whiskey, Dele Omotunde, Dare Babarinsa, and a few others left Newswatch to found TELL magazine. Good journalism is like playing in an orchestra, all hands must work together to produce good music. Working in silos does not work for smooth news production, either electronic or print.

Many Media, Less News

But what do we have today? Any journalist (reporter, editor, sometimes even advert executives) who loses his/her job or in newsroom politics rushes to his/her keyboard and begins to ‘publish online.’ What results from this? Poorly edited and reported ‘news stories,’ some of which are copied from the website of the few remaining legacy media that are still doing the real job. In communication, we talk about plurality of voices. However, what we have today are many news sources with the same news or no news at all! They all publish news from same sources with little or no difference.

A one man ‘Online’ news medium based in Lagos gives you what he calls “Breaking News” about terrorist attacks in Borno State while sitting prettily behind his keyboard in his home in far-flung Lambe or Ota in Ogun State! Meanwhile he has no single reporter out there at the epicentre of the crisis. All what he does is to surf from one (legacy media) website to the other trying to cobble together the few details he can gather to fill the space. Today, news websites are run with no on the ground reporting as was the case in the past. They only copy from the legacy media which also have no more in house reporters but make do with stringers or freelancers who are paid according to number of stories published!

Column writing that was the forte of the likes of Ray Ekpu, Dan Agbese, Mohammed Haruna, Onome Osifo-Whiskey, Yakubu Mohammed, Olatunji Dare, Sonala Olumhense, Dare Babarinsa, etc., are today dominated by those who should still be learning how to write long features on the hitherto ebullient Features Desk of yore. Everyone who can sit in front of a keyboard wants to be given some space and be addressed as a columnist!!!

Nigerian journalists now work in silos – a good reporter wants to be an editor, even if he’s not a good one. Editing is a craft and a talent that you hone over a long period; so is reporting. You can be a great editor but a disaster as a reporter. In the 1980s and 1990s Giwa, Ekpu, Agbese, Mohammed did not set out to establish their medium as individuals, they combined to give Nigeria and the world a solid news magazine. The same happened when Igiebor and others joined forces to found TELL.

Today, every unemployed or unemployable journalist wants to carry a ‘dignified’ title of being a publisher, hence the rash of poorly edited and managed online publications in the cyberspace. It has become a case of ‘read one and you’ve read all’; no variety, no nuance, and no depth. News stories now read the same and flat! Features have become tasteless and investigation poor, if any.

The Legacy Media Too

The legacy media are not faring any better, as some of their managers seem to be afraid of experience, thus old reliable hands are shown the way out and green horns, who should be learning the ropes, are recruited with the salary of an experienced reporter/editor shared into two or three, in order to employ those wet behind their ears, who before long are promoted to editorial seats without the requisite cognate experience. The more the merrier, with merit sacrificed at the altar of cutting corners.

Column writing that was the forte of the likes of Ray Ekpu, Dan Agbese, Mohammed Haruna, Onome Osifo-Whiskey, Yakubu Mohammed, Olatunji Dare, Sonala Olumhense, Dare Babarinsa, etc., are today dominated by those who should still be learning how to write long features on the hitherto ebullient Features Desk of yore. Everyone who can sit in front of a keyboard wants to be given some space and be addressed as a columnist!!!

Newspapers – both online and physical – have become dead; no one wants to read them again, because they are filled with shallow pro-government stories about Governor A and B ‘commissioning’ fathom projects and inspecting or flagging off road construction and fly over bridges, even where there are no rivers or traffic to necessitate such.

Court cases are poorly reported because there are no more experienced court reporters and judicial editors in the news rooms. Gone are the days when The Guardian, Vanguard, Concord, The PUNCH and the others reported the courts robustly and shorn the judgements of all legalese. Today, a court gives a verdict on a case. Wait for the report in the media, and if 10 websites report the verdict, be sure of getting either 10 different (often poor) interpretations or worse still, the same wrong interpretations!! Why?

Investigative stories are hard to come by today because no one is interested in doing them or media managers are not ready to fund or allow reporters engage in such again.

Why can’t TV, radio producers, presenters and others come together to found a powerful YouTube or podcast channel that would be professionally produced and organised, rather than every John and Olumide trying to work in silos and thus producing substandard materials that cannot stand the test of time? Where are the journalists of today who would give us in the cyberspace the equivalent of Newswatch, TELL and other legacy magazines and newspapers?

Ego Massaging as Interviews

Besides, journalists no longer ask troubling questions. We allow politicians to purchase airtime and assemble those who would never ask ‘annoying’ questions, because we want to massage egos and not to interview! The interviewee now calls the shot. A case of the tail wagging the dog.

We all believe the Internet has killed or is killing newspaper readership. I think this is half-true. I have travelled around the world and I still see people buying and holding copies of newspapers, even in climes where there are free WiFi to log unto and read freely. There are still some people who are addicted to holding and reading physical newspapers! The truth is that readers are not getting value for their money and they are therefore running away from paying for public relations couched as news.

The new rave now are YouTube and podcasts. Both have become popular. Our colleagues with or without experience are drifting toward it and are populating the cyberspace with half-baked YouTube and podcast materials. What stops us from learning from the example of Ray Ekpu and the others? Why can’t reporters, sub-editors, features writers and investigative journalists with cognate experience pool resources together and establish a strong online medium, rather than populate the cyberspace with badly sourced news stories on the altar of being called “Online Publishers”?

Why can’t TV, radio producers, presenters and others come together to found a powerful YouTube or podcast channel that would be professionally produced and organised, rather than every John and Olumide trying to work in silos and thus producing substandard materials that cannot stand the test of time? Where are the journalists of today who would give us in the cyberspace the equivalent of Newswatch, TELL and other legacy magazines and newspapers?

For instance, at the completion of this year’s hajj process, seven pilgrims were arrested on their return from the religious rites. It was hot news for all media outlets. What has happened since then? There is also the Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council (PFIPC) scandal. What our numerous news sites have been feeding us with are official statements and no independent investigations!

We need more credible medium online to follow in the footsteps of Premium Times, The Cable, International Centre for Investigative Reports (ICIR), and SaharaReporters, sans the politics of the publisher.

Olayinka Oyegbile is a journalist, writer and media scholar.

World.title: Children honour late Ogun politician with sanitation exercise at Lusada Market
World.content:
The children of late Ogun State politician Aina Taiwo have explained their decision to mark his remembrance with community service rather than a conventional memorial ceremony.

The family partnered with DLAP Academy to organise an environmental sanitation exercise and flash mob at Lusada Market in Igbesa, Ogun State, turning the occasion into a community-focused initiative.

The children said the decision was inspired by their father’s commitment to grassroots development and his relationship with people in the community.

“Our father believed that leadership is measured by service to others. We are honoring him by doing something that benefits the community he loved. His legacy is not only in our memories but in every positive action inspired by his life.” the family said in a joint statement.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The exercise brought together volunteers, youth leaders, traders and residents who cleaned parts of the market while raising awareness about environmental sanitation.

The programme also featured a flash mob by DLAP Academy and BADAGRY BOIZ, with dance and other creative performances used to engage members of the public and promote civic responsibility.

The late Aina Taiwo, who began his journey in Igbesa, was active in politics and served as a councillor. His activities, however, extended beyond public office, with the politician also involved in commercial activities and support for traders and families in the area.

He was remembered by associates as a grassroots politician who maintained close ties with ordinary residents and supported people through mentorship and personal assistance.

The family said the community outreach was intended to reflect that aspect of his life while giving young people an opportunity to participate in an activity with direct benefits for their environment.

DLAP Academy, a youth-led organisation involved in leadership development, community service and creative advocacy, said the collaboration showed how young people could contribute to community development.

The organisation said the combination of sanitation and creative performances provided an avenue to educate residents while making civic participation more engaging.

Some community members welcomed the initiative, describing it as a practical way of commemorating a man whose activities were closely associated with the grassroots.

For the family, the exercise was also a statement about how they want their father’s memory to be preserved.

Rather than limiting his remembrance to tributes, they said, the family wants to encourage actions that reflect the values he represented.

The sanitation exercise at Lusada Market therefore served as both a memorial and a community intervention, with the organisers hoping it would encourage residents, particularly young people, to take greater responsibility for their surroundings.

For the late politician’s children, the choice of service over ceremony was ultimately about ensuring that their father’s memory continues to benefit the people and community he cared about.

World.title: The federalism that promotes productivity (2), By Dipo Baruwa
World.content:
Ultimately, federalism succeeds not merely because power is decentralised, but because authority, incentives and capability are deliberately aligned to make productivity the basis of political success. When states compete to build institutions, attract investment, develop people and expand their productive frontiers, rivalry becomes developmental. It is through that alignment, not constitutional perfection, that productive capabilities are built, locational comparative advantages emerge and sustainable development becomes possible.

Productive Federalism

Productive federalism is not a race to duplicate identical industrial parks, airports, universities or government-owned enterprises. While such investments are not inherently negative, the use of scarce resources requires a more strategic rather than reactive process through which states identify their economic opportunities, coordinate public and private investment around them, develop the required capabilities, and progressively construct locational advantages. The aim is not competition for appearances but for measurable outcomes.

How many sustainable businesses have been created? How many firms have expanded or reinvested? Has agricultural output per hectare improved? Have logistics costs declined? Are technical institutions producing the skills demanded by local industries? Has the state attracted complementary firms around an emerging sector? Has internally generated revenue expanded because productive activity has increased, rather than merely because taxes and levies have multiplied? This requires capable institutions that can identify external opportunities, connect them to local capabilities and ensure that the benefits become embedded within the domestic economy.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

This distinction is important because Nigeria has sometimes confused productive rivalry with politically motivated aggrandisement. States compete to announce the largest airport, the most imposing government building, the newest university or the most ambitious industrial project, even where the economic foundations required to sustain those initiatives are absent. The result is rivalry in expenditure, rather than in capability.

A productive federation would reward governments not for the scale of their announcements but for the durability of the economic systems they create. Public investment would be judged by whether it reduces production costs, improves access to markets, expands knowledge, raises labour productivity and attracts further private investment. Political success would be increasingly connected to economic outcomes, rather than to the ability to distribute patronage or commission conspicuous projects. Unfortunately, the latter is the lived reality of the Nigerian polity.

What is Behind the Cry of Local Government Autonomy?

This also has implications for the relationship between states and local governments. The same authority–incentive–capability framework that applies between the federal and the state governments must also apply within the states themselves. Nigeria cannot build a genuinely productive federation, while local governments remain institutionally marginal to development.

Many services closest to communities, including basic infrastructure maintenance, local markets, primary healthcare support, community libraries, sanitation, local economic information and aspects of agricultural extension, require functioning local government institutions. Yet state governments have progressively absorbed functions and revenues without always providing a more effective replacement. Authority has become concentrated, accountability has become blurred, and local governments have been left with limited incentives or capability to shape development within their jurisdictions.

States should be able to compare themselves transparently on investment attraction, education quality, healthcare delivery, agricultural productivity, infrastructure maintenance, business survival, internally generated revenue and employment creation. Successful reforms undertaken by one state should be documented and adapted by others. Governors should face not only electoral comparison within their states but developmental comparison across the federation.

The question is, therefore, not simply whether local governments should receive allocations directly. It is whether authority, revenue, responsibility and accountability can be aligned at the level in which particular public services and developmental functions can be performed most effectively. Direct funding without capability and accountability may simply reproduce the same distributive weakness at a lower level. But denying local institutions meaningful authority also removes an important layer of experimentation, information gathering and development implementation – basic ingredients for building the federation’s institutional capability to generate, synthesise, and utilise local economic information for national development.

Productive federalism, therefore, requires clarity about who is responsible for what, the resources available for performing those responsibilities, and the outcomes by which performance will be assessed. Where authority is assigned without financial or administrative capability, failure becomes inevitable. Where revenue is provided without responsibility and accountability, distribution becomes an end in itself.

This is also where institutions such as the Nigeria Governors’ Forum should assume a more developmental role. The Forum should not function principally as a platform for political bargaining with the Federal Government or for coordinating common positions on revenue allocation. It could become an institution for productive peer review among states.

States should be able to compare themselves transparently on investment attraction, education quality, healthcare delivery, agricultural productivity, infrastructure maintenance, business survival, internally generated revenue and employment creation. Successful reforms undertaken by one state should be documented and adapted by others. Governors should face not only electoral comparison within their states but developmental comparison across the federation.

Kenya’s experience with county-level devolution offers a useful, though imperfect, illustration. Counties have increasingly been compared on healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure and service delivery. Rwanda, although not a federation, has used performance contracts to connect subnational administration with measurable outcomes. The lesson for Nigeria is not to copy either country, but to recognise that decentralised authority becomes developmental only when performance is visible, comparable and consequential.

The Federal Government also has an indispensable role. Productive federalism does not imply a weak or indifferent centre. It requires a centre that concentrates on functions that benefit from national coordination: macroeconomic stability, national infrastructure, interstate commerce, competition policy, national standards, external trade relations, security coordination, research and the provision of public goods that individual states cannot efficiently supply alone.

The debate before Nigeria is therefore not simply whether to restructure the federation, but what kind of federalism the country wishes to practise. A federation organised predominantly around distribution will continue to produce political competition for existing wealth. A federation organised around productive capability will encourage competition to create new wealth.

The centre should also generate and distribute economic information, coordinate national and subnational institutions, remove barriers to interstate production and trade, and ensure that equalisation supports minimum standards without extinguishing incentives for subnational initiative.

Redistribution remains necessary. Nigeria’s states possess different resource endowments, populations, revenue capacities and historical advantages. A federation cannot ignore these differences. However, redistribution should provide a foundation from which less-advantaged states can build capabilities; it should not become a permanent substitute for productive effort. Equalisation should enable participation in development, not institutionalise dependence on allocation.

The debate before Nigeria is therefore not simply whether to restructure the federation, but what kind of federalism the country wishes to practise. A federation organised predominantly around distribution will continue to produce political competition for existing wealth. A federation organised around productive capability will encourage competition to create new wealth.

Conclusion

The argument throughout this series has been simple. Many of the constitutional and institutional ingredients for productive federalism already exist within Nigeria’s governance framework. What remains deficient is not merely constitutional design, but the governance architecture needed to align authority, incentives and institutional capability.

As Nigeria approaches another general election cycle, this debate should not be ethnicised or reduced to slogans about “true federalism.” Nor should it become a contest between those who support redistribution and those who advocate production. Every viable federation requires both. The real task is to design a system in which equitable redistribution strengthens rather than weakens the incentive to produce.

Ultimately, federalism succeeds not merely because power is decentralised, but because authority, incentives and capability are deliberately aligned to make productivity the basis of political success. When states compete to build institutions, attract investment, develop people and expand their productive frontiers, rivalry becomes developmental. It is through that alignment, not constitutional perfection, that productive capabilities are built, locational comparative advantages emerge and sustainable development becomes possible.

Dipo Baruwa is a business climate development analyst.

World.title: Oath-taking Video: APC’s Desperate Attempt To Smear Adeleke Will Not Save Him From Defeat, Says Imole Campaign Council
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The Imole Campaign Council has described as laughable and defeatist the attempt by the Osun State All Progressives Congress (APC) Governorship Campaign Council to link Governor Ademola Adeleke to an alleged oath-taking video currently circulating on social media, stating emphatically that the governor has absolutely no connection whatsoever with any such activity.

In a statement issued yesterday by the Chairman, Media Committee, The Imole Campaign Council, Bamidele Salam, said the council is presently examining the authenticity, source and circumstances surrounding the video in question.

According to him, “It is important to state categorically that Governor Ademola Adeleke has neither authorised, participated in, directed nor endorsed the taking of any oath by anyone in relation to the August 15 governorship election or for any other political purpose.

“Governor Adeleke is a democrat who believes fundamentally in the freedom of citizens to make their political choices according to their conscience. He does not need oaths, threats, intimidation or any form of coercion to secure the support of the people of Osun State.”

He further said, “Indeed, the governor enjoys broad and demonstrable support across the state based on his record of performance and his personal connection with the people. His campaign is therefore anchored on his achievements, his vision for Osun and the confidence of the electorate, not on superstition, coercion or clandestine practices.

“The APC’s attempt to immediately attribute an unverified social media video to Governor Adeleke is therefore nothing but a hard-sell political manoeuvre by an opposition that is increasingly confronted with the reality of its rejection by the Osun electorate.

“The APC’s attempt to convert an unverified video into a campaign issue also exposes the poverty of its campaign strategy. Rather than engage Governor Adeleke’s administration on roads, healthcare, education, workers’ welfare, infrastructure, rural development and other measurable areas of governance, the opposition has resorted to allegations based on videos whose provenance remains unclear.

“But let there be no ambiguity: Governor Ademola Adeleke does not require anybody to swear an oath before supporting him. He does not require anyone to invoke a curse before voting for him. He does not require supernatural intervention to win an election. His strength is the people. His campaign is based on his record. His mandate belongs to the electorate.”

Salam noted that the APC should therefore stop looking for excuses in videos and begin preparing for the verdict of the Osun people on August 15.

“The people of Osun are not being asked to vote for Governor Adeleke because of any oath. They are being asked to vote for him because they have seen the difference between a government that works for the people and an opposition that has offered little beyond fear, propaganda and empty accusations.

“Governor Adeleke will face the people on August 15 with his record. Let the APC face the people with its own record.”

World.title: Benue ADC Guber Candidate Confident Atiku Will Win 2027 Presidential Election
World.content:
George Okoh in Makurdi

The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Benue State, Herman Hembe, has declared that the ADC’s presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, will win the 2027 election.

Hembe disclosed this in Makurdi yesterday while unveiling his deputy, John Abba.

He had constituted a committee to select the party deputy governorship candidate a few days after he emerged as the party’s gubernatorial candidate.

According to Hembe, the selection of deputy governorship candidate which has the endorsement of the national chairman of the party, Senator David Mark, was transparent.

Hembe said, “Let me congratulate Abba on his selection as deputy governorship candidate of the party. We constituted a team to consult and get the deputy governorship candidate and our leader, David Mark ensured the process was transparent.”

Speaking on the permutations, Hembe stated that all things are working in favour of the party presidential candidate.

“Our permutations are that the votes from the Southern part of the country will be shared between Peter Obi and Bola Tinubu and we are very sure that none of Obi and Tinubu will be able to defeat Atiku in the three geo political zones in the North,” Hembe said.

While charging the party members to go all out to work for all the party candidates at the presidential election, Hembe assured that there will be band wagon effects on the second election.

“Our hardest job is to work and ensure that our party wins the presidential and National Assembly elections, then, we will just go and sleep because that victory will have a positive effect on our election.”

Hembe promised that he is only going to spend a term in office to complete the eight years of Jechira Zone and create history to hand over to the Benue South senatorial district, known as Zone C.

World.title: 2027: Kogi East APC Stakeholders Back Tinubu, Ododo, Demand Power Rotation
World.content:
• Say East will no longer be appendage to any political bloc

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general election, critical stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kogi East Senatorial District have declared their total support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, while demanding a fresh and equitable framework for political power rotation in Kogi State.

The stakeholders, who spoke through a communiqué issued at the end of their Strategic Leadership Conference in Abuja and made available to THISDAY on Saturday, said Kogi East would no longer accept a political arrangement that relegated the senatorial district to the status of an appendage of another political bloc.

They also called for direct negotiations with political stakeholders from Kogi Central and Kogi West on what they described as “distinct, transparent and equitable” terms to establish a predictable framework for power transition and inclusive development in the state.

The stakeholders said their immediate priority was to ensure victory for the APC in the January/February 2027 general election, particularly the re-election of Tinubu and the victory of all APC candidates contesting National and State Assembly seats.

They further pledged to mobilise support for Governor Ododo’s re-election for a second term in the November 2027 governorship election.

According to them, the political objective was not merely to win elections but to reposition Kogi East within the mainstream of state and national politics and secure what they described as the “deserved share of development” for the district.

The communiqué noted that Kogi East had recorded the highest bloc vote for President Tinubu among the three senatorial districts of Kogi State in the 2023 presidential election, stressing that the district was prepared to increase its contribution to the APC in 2027.

He said: “We look forward to increasing our electoral contributions to the APC and to strengthening our collaboration with our fellow compatriots from Kogi Central and Kogi West Senatorial Districts to return power to Kogi East.

“However, we are resolved to mobilise total support for the incumbent governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, and his re-election for his second term come

2027.”

The declaration came against the backdrop of what the stakeholders described as more than a decade of political fractures, disaffection and missed opportunities in Kogi State following the 2015 governorship election and the death of the late former governor, Prince Abubakar Audu.

They said attempts to achieve political realignment in 2019 and 2023 were not sustained, leaving ordinary citizens of Kogi East to bear the consequences of prolonged political disagreements.

The stakeholders insisted that the time had come to heal the wounds, rebuild trust among the three senatorial districts and establish a new political understanding based on equity, inclusion and mutual respect.

They said: “We refuse to allow old wounds to permanently damage the deep historical linkages between the people of the various sections of Kogi State.

“Our only path to reawaken the political strength of Kogi East is to encourage healthy collaboration with the other sections of the state and negotiate truthfully for all that our people deserve.

“We reject any attempt to make Kogi East an appendage of any group in the state.”

The stakeholders invoked the political legacy of Prince Audu, saying his philosophy was anchored on statewide unity, inclusion, dialogue and equitable distribution of development.

They recalled that during Audu’s administration, major projects were conceived and executed across the three senatorial districts, including the establishment of the state university in Anyigba and the Obajana Cement Project, as well as roads and other civic infrastructure.

They argued that the late governor’s political philosophy should be revived as the foundation for a new era of cooperation in Kogi State.

“That is the true political philosophy we must revive today: vision, selflessness, courage, fraternity, equity and shared purpose,” the communiqué stated.

The stakeholders also demanded an immediate shift towards a predictable political transition arrangement, arguing that sustainable development could not be achieved where political succession remained a source of tension.

According to them, “We assemble here today to lay a solid foundation for Kogi East to be part of a realistic, predictable and harmonious political transition in Kogi State.

“We call for an immediate shift towards building consensus, renegotiating power transfer and rotation, and establishing an inclusive, development-driven agenda that guarantees equitable access to the instruments of power.”

The group also sought national recognition for Audu, describing him as a statesman whose contribution to Nigeria’s democratic development should not be confined to his final years in politics.

It urged the Kogi State Government to present Audu’s contributions to the Federal Government for a “highly merited and long-overdue national honour”.

The stakeholders cited the 10th anniversary commemorative events held in Lokoja in October 2025, which brought together national political leaders, traditional rulers and former governors, as evidence of the late governor’s enduring national stature.

They also noted the naming of a major boulevard in Lokoja after Audu by Governor Ododo and the unveiling of the Prince Abubakar Audu Leadership Foundation by the representative of President Tinubu at the anniversary events.

The stakeholders called for the foundation to operate as a nationwide, non-partisan platform for preserving Audu’s memory and promoting his leadership philosophy.

They argued that restricting his legacy to one election cycle or the final period of his political career would amount to historical injustice.

“Prince Audu belonged to multiple eras of Nigeria’s democratic development, from his early public service to his trailblazing leadership as the first and second civilian executive governor.

He must be remembered as a statesman,” they said.

In their resolutions, the stakeholders pledged to unify APC grassroots structures across the nine local government areas of Kogi East behind Tinubu and all APC legislative candidates in the 2027 elections.

They also committed themselves to dialogue with political leaders in Kogi Central and Kogi West, stressing that such engagement must be conducted on mutually acceptable and equitable terms.

The stakeholders further resolved to align with the state government to promote peace, inclusivity and accelerated development across Kogi East.

They called on party leaders, youth leaders, elders and other members of the late Audu’s political family to put past grievances aside and work towards a united political front.

“Our goal is to reintegrate Kogi East into the mainstream of politics in Kogi State and the nation on terms that will assure us of our deserved share of development,” they declared.

World.title: Idris Deserves Second Term, Says Zuru, Urges Voters To Support Gov For Continuity
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent

The Special Adviser to the Kebbi State Governor on Media Strategy and Communication, Abdullahi Zuru, has declared that Governor Nasir Idris has performed credibly well and deserves to be re-elected for a second term in 2027.

Zuru made the declaration yesterday while responding to questions from journalists who paid him a courtesy visit. He said the assessment was based on the governor’s record of delivery across key sectors since assuming office in 2023.

“Since the creation of Kebbi State, we have never had it this good,” Zuru said. “The governor has touched every sector and the impact is visible to the people.”

According to him, the Idris administration has prioritised the economy, infrastructural development, education, health, workers’ welfare, and human capital development. He noted that the interventions were designed to directly improve the lives of ordinary citizens.

On infrastructure, the media aide said the government has embarked on road projects, urban renewal, and rural development programmes aimed at opening up communities and boosting commerce across the 21 local government areas of the state.

“In education and health, we have seen massive investments in schools, primary healthcare centres, and the welfare of teachers and health workers,” he added. “Workers’ salaries are paid as and when due, and their welfare is receiving serious attention.”

Zuru further stated that the governor’s approach to governance has restored public confidence in government. He said the administration runs an open-door policy that allows citizens to feel the presence of government at all levels.

Calling on voters in the state, he urged them to rally behind the governor ahead of the next election. “I encourage the good people of Kebbi State to support Governor Nasir Idris and ensure he returns for a second term so that the good work can continue,” he said.

The Special Adviser also took a swipe at some politicians in the state, saying they lacked the pedigree to challenge the governor’s record.

“Some of them have held positions at state and federal levels before, yet they have no track record to show for it,” Zuru stated. “Leadership is about results, and the results are there for everyone to see.”

He noted that with the current momentum, Kebbi is on the path of sustainable development, and continuity under Governor Idris remains the best option for the people of the state.

World.title: Beyond Interest: The Alternative Bank Charts New Path for Wealth Creation
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Alternative Bank has concluded plans to chart a new course for capital allocation in Nigeria as it hosted investors, policymakers and business leaders in Lagos under the theme, ‘Beyond Interest: Capital, Innovation, and the Future of Wealth’.

The event focused on non-interest finance and the need to deploy patient capital into the country’s productive sectors rather than extractive models that only generate short-term gains.

Opening the forum, Muhtar Bakare, Chairman of The Alternative Bank, said the economy must move away from capital that merely harvests value.

“Extractive capital treats the economy chiefly as a place from which value is harvested. It may reward its owner, but it rarely leaves the economy stronger. Productive capital invests in enterprises, assets and systems that grow over time. It creates income for workers, demand for suppliers, revenue for governments and sustainable returns for investors,” Bakare stated.

Delivering the keynote on behalf of Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, the Commissioner for Finance, Abayomi Oluyomi, said government has a critical role in de-risking investment through infrastructure and credible policy.

He cited the Blue and Red Line rail projects as examples of public investment expanding markets and reducing business costs.

“The future of finance will belong to capital that is more purposeful, innovative and closely connected to productive economic activity.

“The future of development finance will increasingly draw on instruments including green bonds, sukuk and other ethical and non-interest structures that connect capital to real assets, productive activity and measurable outcomes. Investors do not invest in government promises. They invest in credible systems,” he said.

Also speaking, former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Raji Fashola, urged financial institutions to prioritise investments tied to tangible assets and community well-being over those chasing immediate profits, noting that such investments deliver more lasting social and economic returns.

The forum featured expert briefings from Abubakar Suleiman, Board Member of Sterling Financial Holdings and a promoter of non-interest banking in Nigeria; Dr. Stanley Jacob, Group Chief, Innovation and Technology at Meristem; and Ajibola Tobi-Osho, Executive Director of Tugrande Alliance Limited.

Their presentations covered the business case for ethical capital, the potential of pan-African payment systems and asset tokenisation, and Nigeria’s macroeconomic outlook.

The discussions reinforced The Alternative Bank’s position that building a resilient Nigerian economy requires shared-risk, non-interest financial structures that give investors confidence and ensure investments create cross-generational value.

The bank said it will continue to champion financial models that link capital directly to real assets and productive activity as part of its mandate to drive inclusive and sustainable wealth creation.

World.title: Abia Leadership Academy, Strategic Institution For Training Future Leaders, Says Gov
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti, says the Abia State Leadership Academy was established as a strategic institution where ethics, values, and practical leadership skills would be instilled in Abia youths.

He said the essence was to catch them young, adding “we are committed to getting it right with the younger generation. Otherwise, our wider development efforts will be in jeopardy.”

Governor Otti, represented by his Deputy, Engr. Ikechukwu Emetu, spoke while declaring open the 2026 Youth Leadership Bootcamp of the Abia State Leadership Academy. The batch has 1, 000 participants selected from 7, 000 applicants. The training holds every long vacation at Government College, Umuahia, since the Otti administration came to power.

The governor reaffirmed his commitment to developing young Abians as future leaders of the state and nation and charged the participants to learn with humility and participate actively in the programme.

“This year’s programme is particularly significant, with 1,000 participants selected from more than 7,000 applicants. That response tells us our young people are hungry for genuine transformation—and they trust this administration to deliver it.

“For 2026, we’ve partnered with the Enterprise Development Centre of Pan-Atlantic University—a global-standard institution with ties to the World Bank, Goldman Sachs, and MasterCard.

“To our young participants, your selection is only the beginning. I urge you to learn with humility, participate actively, build meaningful relationships and, most importantly, use what you learn to positively influence your schools, communities and State,” the Governor said.

Earlier, the facilitator of the programme and Chairman of Abia State Civil Service Commission, Pastor Mrs. Eno Jerry –Eze, represented by Rev. Mrs. Ifeoma Agu, said that the programme was an opportunity to for the youths to imbibe the ideals of civic responsibility and urged the participants to be determined to use the lessons of the bootcamp to better their lives as well as bring about the change they crave for.

Mrs. Jerry-Eze thanked the governor for placing the youths in the leadership map in Nigeria and for leaving a legacy that assures that the leadership he has introduced would be sustained.

Delivering a lecture on the theme of the training: ‘The Demands of Stewardship’, the Chief of Staff to the Governor, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, noted that the governor was investing in the lives of the teenagers and young leaders of the state through the academy.

Pastor Ajagba, while describing the initiative as a strategic investment in the future of the state and a lasting legacy that will shape the character, mindset and leadership capacity of generations yet unborn, disclosed that by intentionally preparing young people for responsible leadership, Governor Otti was laying a firm foundation for sustainable development and ensuring that the ideals of integrity, innovation and public service remain deeply rooted in Abia’s future.

He added that it was an honour for all those invited to share their perspectives in the noble vision of raising a generation of principled, disciplined and transformational leaders through the academy and applauded the exemplary life of vision, focus, sacrifice, discipline, competence, integrity of Governor Otti and assuring of the unwavering commitment of the Governor to good governance and purposeful leadership.

Also speaking on behalf of the Executive Director of the development partner – the Enterprise Development Centre (EDC), Pan-Athlantic University, Dr. Uche Egbuna, said the future of every society depends on the quality of leaders it intentionally develops, adding that leadership was about responsibility, integrity and service.

Dr. Egbuna stated that the boot camp was built on four key pillars: leadership and service, enterprise, impact and innovation, and encouraged participants to strive for meaningful impact by becoming problem-solvers and change-makers.

He described the partnership with the Abia State Leadership Academy as a shared commitment to developing ethical leaders, resilient entrepreneurs and innovative young people who will contribute to economic growth and social transformation.

President of Abia State Leadership Academy, Prof. Kenneth Kalu, disclosed that 7052 persons applied for the programme and about 1000 were qualified after the rigorous processes of selection.

Prof. Kalu enjoined the participants to remember that they were expected “to think, reflect and become” future leaders, emphasising that what was more important was not that they participated in the programme but what they become from the programme.

Responding on behalf of the participants, Chukwuemerie Obiorah and Treasure Ogbonna thanked the governor for the opportunity given them to become transformational leaders, assuring that they would not disappoint but make good use of the bootcamp to better citizens in the society.

The opening ceremony of the bootcamp being coordinated by the Programme Manager, Abia State Leadership Academy and Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Public Communication, Mr. Dodoh Okafor, was graced by Secretary to the State Government, Dr. Emmanuel Meribeole; Commissioner for Tertiary Education, Prof. Uche Emeh Uche; Principal Secretary and Chief Strategist Officer of the state, Mr. Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, among other government officials.

World.title: Gov Yahaya Receives Report of Taskforce Committee on Reforms, Revitalisation of Basic, Technical Education
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Gombe

Gombe State Governor, Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, yesterday received the report of the Taskforce Committee on the Reforms and Revitalisation of Basic and Technical Education in the state, describing it as a critical blueprint for transforming the education sector.

The governor assured that his administration would immediately commence the implementation of the committee’s recommendations as part of its commitment to repositioning basic and technical education for greater efficiency, improved learning outcomes and the development of a skilled, future-ready workforce.

He stated this while receiving the report presented by a member of the committee and foremost educationist, Mr. Mataimaki Tom Maiyashi, alongside the Commissioner of Education, Associate Professor Aishatu Umar Maigari who chaired the Taskforce.

Governor Yahaya stated that his administration remains resolute in its commitment to strengthening the education sector through bold policy decisions and structural reforms that will ensure sustainable development in line with the state’s 10-year development agenda (DEVAGOM).

“On the report, I want to assure you that we are not going to abandon this document. We shall study it immediately and begin implementation of the recommendations,” the governor said.

He disclosed that his administration has already commenced far-reaching structural adjustments in the education sector, citing the recent merger of the Ministry of Higher Education with the Ministry of Education into a single ministry as one of the first major reform initiatives.

“We will do structural adjustments in the education sector. I can even say that we have started because I have now merged the Ministry of Higher Education and the Ministry of Education to become one ministry, which is what is obtainable even at the federal level. This will strengthen coordination, improve policy implementation and enhance service delivery across all levels of education,” he stated.

Reflecting on the progress recorded since assuming office in 2019, Yahaya noted that his administration inherited an education sector confronted by numerous challenges but has, through sustained strategic interventions, recorded remarkable achievements in infrastructure, teacher development, school enrolment, access to quality education and institutional reforms.

“We knew how we met this sector when we came into office in 2019, and we thank God that we have been able to achieve so much. I want to reiterate the pledge I made that we will leave Gombe better than we met it in the education sector. That commitment remains unwavering, and we shall continue to invest in reforms that will guarantee quality education for our children and future generations,” the governor stated.

Speaking on behalf of the committee, foremost educationist and former Commissioner for Education in Kaduna State, Mr. Maiyashi, commended Governor Yahaya for his visionary leadership and foresight in establishing the taskforce.

He observed that the governor’s investments and numerous achievements in the education sector have already laid a strong foundation for sustainable development.

He described the committee’s report as an honest reflection of the realities confronting basic and technical education in Gombe State.

Maiyashi assured the governor that the recommendations are practical, realistic and fully implementable, urging him to earnestly begin the implementation of what the document recommends.

He expressed confidence that the faithful implementation of the recommendations would significantly transform the state’s education system and position Gombe as a model for educational excellence.

Earlier, the Commissioner for Education, Prof. Maigari, who chaired the Taskforce, explained that the committee was inaugurated in November 2025 with the mandate to critically assess the state of basic and technical education in Gombe State, develop actionable strategies, recommend practical reforms capable of restoring the lost glory of the state’s schools, and address all issues incidental to its assignment.

According to her, the committee’s work focused on key thematic areas including teacher-related challenges, infrastructure deficits, governance and administration, student welfare and learning conditions, as well as security and community-related issues affecting schools.

She explained that the findings from these assessments formed the basis of the committee’s recommendations, which were carefully packaged into eight priority reform clusters requiring immediate government intervention to accelerate improvements in the education sector.

The commissioner expressed appreciation to Governor Inuwa Yahaya for demonstrating exceptional political will and commitment to education by constituting a high-powered committee of renowned professionals whose wealth of experience enriched the quality of the report.

The Taskforce Committee comprised eminent education experts and policymakers, including Prof. Maigari, the Gombe State Commissioner for Education; Dr. Yakubu, former Executive Secretary of the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE); Dr. Hamid Bobboyi, former Executive Secretary of the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC); Mr. Maiyashi, education consultant and former Commissioner for Education in Kaduna State; Dr. Sadiq Gombe, and also the Executive Chairman of the State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB); and the Permanent Secretary, Special Services and Political (SS & POL), Government House, Gombe.

World.title: Just In: DSS Arrests Three More Suspects Over Kidnap of Nasarawa Varsity Professor
World.content:
Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) have arrested three more suspects linked to the kidnapping of the Dean of Agriculture at Nasarawa State University, Professor Samuel Avengbe Okunsebor.

The suspects were arrested on Friday night at a local brothel along the Mararraban Akunza axis of the Lafia–Makurdi highway.

A security source disclosed that the three suspects were members of the kidnapping gang responsible for the abduction of the university don.

Professor Okunsebor was kidnapped by gunmen in the early hours of Wednesday, July 15, 2026, at Mile Uku, a border community between Lafia and Nasarawa-Eggon Local Government Areas of Nasarawa State.

He was rescued two days later by DSS operatives. Two suspects, including a woman, were also arrested in connection with the incident at the time.

According to a security source, the newly arrested suspects were identified as 25-year-old Yakubu Abubakar, also known as Black or Starboy, a member of the Doemak tribe in Plateau State; 37-year-old Usman Abubakar Mairiga; and 27-year-old Sale Babauro Abubakar.

The source said Mairiga is Hausa, while Sale Babauro Abubakar is Fulani.

The three suspects are currently being held at the DSS State Command for further investigation.

The source added that their continued detention followed a warrant obtained from a magistrate’s court.

The latest arrests bring to five the number of suspects reportedly apprehended in connection with the kidnapping of Professor Okunsebor. Investigations into the incident are ongoing.

World.title: Pitso Back! SAFA set to announce Mosimane as new Bafana coach next week
World.content:
Pitso Mosimane is set to make a sensational return to Bafana Bafana after the SAFA National Executive Committee (NEC) approved his appointment as the new head coach.

The South African Football Association (SAFA) held an Extraordinary NEC Meeting at SAFA House on Saturday, where members backed Mosimane to take over from Hugo Broos.

Broos stepped down from his position earlier this week after guiding Bafana Bafana through an historic period, including their return to the FIFA World Cup.



Pitso Mosimane to take over Bafana once again

While Mosimane’s appointment has been approved, SAFA says there are still a few matters to be finalised before the former Mamelodi Sundowns coach is officially unveiled.

“The NEC has approved the appointment of coach Pitso to Bafana Bafana, but we still need to tie up some loose ends. We will make a formal announcement of the coach next week,” SAFA president Dr Danny Jordaan said following Saturday’s meeting.

Mosimane’s return would mark a new chapter for the 61-year-old, who previously led Bafana Bafana between 2010 and 2012.



The former Sundowns mentor has also enjoyed considerable success at club level, most notably guiding the Tshwane giants to domestic dominance and continental glory before taking charge of Egyptian giants Al Ahly.

Bafana Bafana, meanwhile, are coming off an historic FIFA World Cup campaign.

The national team qualified for the tournament for the first time in 24 years and went on to reach the knockout stages for the first time in their history.



Their memorable campaign included a 1-0 victory over South Korea in Monterrey, Mexico, with Thapelo Maseko scoring the only goal of the match.

Attention now turns to the next chapter under Mosimane, with SAFA expected to formally confirm his appointment as Bafana head coach next week.

The NEC meeting also covered preparations for SAFA’s Elective Congress, which is scheduled to take place on 12 September 2026.



Nominations for the various positions to be contested at the congress were handed over to the Governance Committee this week.

Are you a fan of Jingles?

World.title: Five things we learned from Orlando Pirates’ MTN8 win over Durban City
World.content:
Orlando Pirates edged Durban City 2-1 after extra time in the opening MTN8 quarter-final on Saturday afternoon.

Despite securing their place in the semi-finals, the Buccaneers will not be entirely satisfied with their performance.

Pirates struggled to break down a stubborn Durban City defence, even after being handed a numerical advantage. After Poggenpoel was shown a red card for a foul on Tshepang Moremi, it appeared that the Buccaneers would cruise to victory.



However, City responded shortly after half-time and continued to fight as though they still had 11 players on the pitch.

Pirates MTN8 struggles a concern this season

Pirates created several chances, but once again struggled to convert them. This was a problem for the club throughout last season, and their inability to address it was evident against Durban City.

Head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou introduced the likes of Oswin Appollis, Yanela Mbuthuma and Patrick Maswanganyi. Still, the substitutions failed to make the desired impact as Pirates were eventually dragged into extra time.



The winning goal finally arrived in the final minute of extra time when new signing Ghampani Lungu found the back of the net to send Pirates into the semi-finals.

Here are the major lessons from Orlando Pirates’ victory in the MTN8.

Pirates still struggle from set pieces

Pirates usually win more than 10 set-piece opportunities in a match, but they often fail to turn those chances into genuine goal-scoring opportunities.



Against Durban City, the Buccaneers won more than 20 corners, yet very few of them caused any real problems for the opposition goalkeeper.

Ironically, their decisive goal came from a corner, with Lungu finding space after City failed to mark him properly.

The lack of quality delivery and finishing from set pieces remains a concern. It is an area Pirates will need to improve, particularly with the CAF Champions League ahead.



Pirates looked ordinary in the MTN8 quarter-finals

Kabelo Kgositsile shows promise

Among the new players introduced, Kabelo Kgositsile was one of the most impressive.

The youngster looked lively and threatened the Durban City defence on several occasions. His pace and movement caused problems and gave Pirates another attacking outlet.



Some of the other new arrivals, however, failed to make the same impact. They appeared a level below established players such as Thalente Mbatha and Tshepang Moremi.

Lungu, in particular, struggled for much of the match, but his late winner showed the quality he possesses. Scoring such an important goal could also provide him with a much-needed confidence boost.

Thabiso Sesane’s departure could hurt Pirates



With Nkosinathi Sibisi injured, Ouaddou was forced to make changes in central defence and brought in Mpho Chabatsane.

His partnership with Lebone Seema raised questions, particularly after City managed to score soon after the defensive changes.

Pirates may have been better served keeping Thabiso Sesane, who could have been allowed to impress during the second half of last season.



Had Sesane remained at the club throughout pre-season, he would also have had more time to develop an understanding with Seema.

Given his quality and experience, Sesane could have provided Pirates with another option in defence, especially in a match where they had a numerical advantage for such a long period.

Oswin Appollis’ form remains a concern

Coming into the match, Appollis was seen as Pirates top player and maybe one of the contenders for Last Man Stadning in the MTN8.



Appollis has struggled for form since the FIFA World Cup and once again failed to make a significant impact against Durban City.

The winger was largely ineffective during the match, but considering the lack of impact from some of the substitutes, Pirates may have benefited from keeping him on the pitch.

His lack of creativity and goals has become a concern, particularly when Pirates are dominating possession but struggling to find a way through compact defences.



The Buccaneers will need more from one of their key attacking players as the season progresses.

More struggles upfront for Pirates

Radipane is not the solution

Boitumelo Radipane came on for Yanela Mbuthuma and saw plenty of the ball, but once again failed to provide the cutting edge Pirates needed.



Looking comfortable in possession is not enough for a striker. The primary responsibility is to create clear opportunities and, most importantly, score goals.

Radipane had a late opportunity to seal the victory when he was presented with a chance to make it 3-1, but his effort went straight at the goalkeeper.

Pirates supporters have already expressed frustration with both Radipane and Mbuthuma over their inability to convert chances in the MTN8 quarter-final.



With the CAF Champions League also on the horizon, Pirates may need to consider investing in a proven top-class striker if they want to compete on multiple fronts.

World.title: New Orlando Pirates signing hits late volley to dump Durban City out of MTN8
World.content:
Orlando Pirates came back behind after Durban City cancelled out Patrick Maswanganyi’s first-half penalty. Lungu eventually produced the decisive moment with a powerful volley in the final stages of extra time.

PATRICK MASWANGANYI BREAKS THE DEADLOCK

Orlando Pirates started with attacking intent but struggled to find a breakthrough in the opening stages. Thalente Mbatha tested Sangare from distance, while Tshepang Moremi came closest when his free-kick struck the crossbar.

Durban City also threatened on the counter. Lubumba broke forward and fired wide, while Mbuthuma missed a good opportunity after Maswanganyi delivered a dangerous cross.



The game changed in the 33rd minute. Poggenpoel brought down Moremi inside the box. The Durban City defender received a second yellow card and left his team with 10 players.

Maswanganyi stepped up and calmly converted the penalty. He sent Sangare the wrong way to give the Buccaneers a 1-0 lead. The Buccaneers took that advantage into the break.

Durban City responded after half-time despite playing with 10 men. Lubumba levelled in the 52nd minute after Shandu and Gaston Sirino combined effectively on the right. The visitors then defended resolutely as Pirates searched for another goal.

Sangare saved Appollis’ free-kick and later denied Moremi inside the box. Kgositsile also came close for Durban City, but his header flew narrowly wide.

Neither side found a winner in normal time.

Also read: Latest report: SAFA find new Bafana Bafana coach



GHAMPANI LUNGU GRABS LATE WINNER FOR ORLANDO PIRATES

Extra time produced another intense battle.

Moremi struck the crossbar with a free-kick early in the additional period. Domingo then curled an effort towards goal, but Sipho Chaine positioned himself well to make the save.

Durban City continued to threaten through Morris, but Seema showed impressive pace to recover and clear the danger.

Pirates increased the pressure during the second half of extra time.

Radiopane forced another save from Sangare, while Lungu saw an effort stopped by the goalkeeper. Mbatha also tested the Durban City defence with a powerful shot from distance.

Then came the decisive moment.

In the 29th minute of extra time, Lungu unleashed a powerful volley inside the box. Sangare had no chance as the ball crashed into the net. Orlando Pirates held on to win 2-1 and booked their place in the MTN8 semi-finals.

The Buccaneers remain on course for a historic fifth consecutive MTN8 title.

World.title: LIVE | WAFCON: Banyana Banyana v Morocco
World.content:
Banyana Banyana are one victory away from qualifying for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup after booking their place in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations. Image: SAFA website

Banyana Banyana are just one victory away from qualifying for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil after booking their place in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Burkina Faso.

Thembi Kgatlana scored the decisive goal in the first half as South Africa secured second place in Group B to advance to the knockout stages, where they will face tournament hosts Morocco in Rabat on Saturday, 8 August.

Kick-off is at 22:00 (SA time).



A place in the semi-finals will also secure qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

South Africa finished the group stage on four points, three behind group winners Ivory Coast, who defeated Tanzania 2-1 in the other Group B fixture.

Desiree Ellis praises grit over glamour

Banyana Banyana coach Desiree Ellis admitted her side made life difficult for themselves after taking an early lead but was delighted with the resilience they showed to grind out the result.

“I said it was going to be a tough one, and we made it a little bit difficult for ourselves. We scored early and stopped playing,” Ellis said.

“You’ve got to give credit to the players though, it wasn’t pretty and sometimes it doesn’t have to be pretty. Defensively we were organised and I think we had one or two chances that could have put the game to bed, but I thought the team played very well.”

Ellis made two changes to the side that drew with Ivory Coast, bringing Isabella Ludwig and Hildah Magaia into the starting line-up in place of Bongeka Gamede and Nthabiseng Majiya.



The victory completed an impressive turnaround after the defending African champions opened their campaign with a defeat to Tanzania before drawing with Ivory Coast.

“It’s not how you start, but how you finish,” Ellis said.

“The fightback shows what this team is made of, and we keep working on being better and that’s all we can do. Now the games are coming thick and fast, there’s no margin for error.

“We have also showed that we can grind out results. I think in 2018 we played probably the best football of the tournament and we didn’t win it. In 2022 we mixed it up, so we’ve learned that you can’t play pretty all the time and that’s what people expect from Banyana Banyana.

“But we will take it step by step and day by day.”

Milestones for Banyana Banyana

There was more reason to celebrate for South Africa beyond qualification.

Captain Refiloe Jane marked her birthday with victory, while Hildah Magaia and Gabriela Moodaly-Salgado both reached the milestone of 50 international caps.

Kgatlana’s match-winning display also earned her the Player of the Match award.

World.title: Teen elated as GoFundMe exceeds R2m: ‘Give and you will receive’
World.content:
Young Wernand has recieved over R2m in a GoFundMe campaign. Images via Instagram

A teen boy known as Wernand, who appeared in a viral BI Phakathi video, has pledged to share the funds raised through a GoFundMe campaign with his family and others living in destitution.

The 14-year-old has received over R2 million in donations from around the world.

GOFUNDME CAMPAIGN SURPASSES R2 MILLION FOR TEEN WERNAND

In recent days, a GoFundMe campaign set up for young Wernand, seen in a BI Phakathi video, has exceeded R2 million.



The campaign has raised $128 200 (over R2 million) from donors around the world.

Wernand touched the hearts of the public after he was spotted gathering scrap metal and old tyres to sell to raise money to help his family. At the time, the 14-year-old lived in a dilapidated house with no walls or roof.

In an updated video, Wernand appeared to be living in a safer home, filled with food and groceries.

The overjoyed teen vowed to continue supporting his mother, baby sister, and all those living in destitution.

He said, “I don’t have the kind of heart to say no. I don’t know how to say no.

“Even if I have a R2 in my pocket….



Wernand added that his grandmother had instilled in him a life lesson to help the less fortunate.

He added, “If you give, you will receive”

WHO IS BI PHAKATHI?

Good Samaritans BI Phakathi and US philanthropist Logan Mayberry are credited for helping young Wernand secure food and a safe home via the GoFundMe account.

While Mayberry is widely known through his Reward The Kind charity endeavour, Phakathi has kept his identity a secret from ordinary South Africans.

Through his foundation, the Phakathi aims to “help people who need help in these difficult times”.

He says of himself: “The South African motivational speaker, filmmaker, and life coach BI Phakathi lends just a hand, without showing his face.

“BI has maintained his reputation as a mysterious giver to the underserved on the streets. In his videos, he helps the underprivileged and homeless people with resources. Bi believes in maintaining anonymity while adding value to society”.

World.title: Mamelodi Sundowns confirm the signing of Bafana Bafana forward
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns have confirmed the signing of Cassius Mailula, with the forward returning to the club after three years away.

The 25-year-old has rejoined the Brazilians after spending the past three years with MLS side Toronto FC.

For weeks, there had been speculation that Mailula could return to Masandawana. With the departure of Peter Shalulile, his return allows the talented striker to finish what he started with the Tshwane giants.



“A familiar face returns to where it all began. Cassius Mailula is back in yellow, ready for a new chapter with The Brazilians. Masandawana, welcome him back in the comments,” Mamelodi Sundowns said on social media.

The Brazilians have been relatively quiet during this transfer window. Following the untimely passing of midfielder Jayden Adams, their pre-season was delayed, meaning they were unable to begin their Betway Premiership campaign last weekend.

Mailula’s arrival gives Sundowns another attacking option and adds more firepower to their frontline. He will compete alongside the likes of Tashreeq Matthews, Iqraam Rayners and Brayan León.

Mamelodi Sundowns re-signs Mailula

Before leaving Sundowns for Toronto FC in July 2023, Mailula enjoyed a breakthrough 2022/23 campaign, scoring 16 goals in 32 appearances across all competitions.

However, he made only a handful of appearances for Toronto before being loaned to Wydad Casablanca, where he played under former Sundowns coach Rulani Mokwena.

His spell in Morocco proved successful, with the forward scoring important goals for the North African giants.



Mailula later had another loan spell in Belgium before eventually returning to Mamelodi Sundowns following the end of his time with Toronto FC.

The Bafana Bafana forward now has an opportunity to revive his career at the club where he first made his name and once again establish himself as one of the country’s most exciting attacking talents.

Will Mailula shine or flop?

World.title: ‘As it was before COVID’: Pensioners push to have payment date reversed
World.content:
SASSA beneficiaries have renewed calls for the agency to shift grant payment dates back to the start of each month, with commenters arguing the current system leaves pensioners short-changed for longer than necessary.

In response to a The South African article, Nola Van Loggerenberg raised the payment date issue head-on, comparing the current system unfavourably with pre-pandemic practice.

“At least the pensioners don’t have to wait 33 days next month for SASSA to pay out. The date should be moved back to the first of every month as it was before COVID,” she wrote.



Money doesn’t stretch far enough

Beyond the date itself, beneficiaries say the money doesn’t last once it hits their accounts. Mary Coetzee summed up the financial squeeze many pensioners face in stark terms: “Yes, that money lasts just one day.” Caroline September agreed the strain begins immediately, adding “Not just one day..up..the moment you take it out”, suggesting that for many, the grant is spent before it even reaches their pockets properly.

Caregiver and disability grant frustrations surface

The thread also surfaced deeper concerns about how SASSA assesses grant applications. Daisy Moodley shared her own experience applying for a caregiver-related grant, describing what she felt was an unreasonable expectation from officials. “OMW, they don’t give the caregiver money, apparently they want to see you in a wheelchair, my doc said yesterday. I went to fill the form saying I look so fit, 76, yet I cannot walk without someone holding me, I have a misbalance, got pins and needles in my knee,” she wrote, a comment that drew sympathetic reactions from other users.

Meanwhile, Machiliza Nomthandazoe raised a separate practical concern, asking for guidance on updating banking details on behalf of an elderly relative: “Plz help what do they need at Sassa my granny want to change her banking details.”



Together, the comments paint a picture of beneficiaries juggling delayed payments, insufficient amounts, and confusing administrative processes, all while trying to make ends meet on a fixed monthly income.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

The Soweto giants enter the clash with history firmly in their sights as they chase a record-breaking fifth consecutive MTN8 title. Orlando Pirates began their remarkable run in 2022, defeating AmaZulu 1-0 in the final. Monnapule Saleng scored the decisive goal to secure the Buccaneers’ first trophy under former coach Jose Riveiro.



They successfully defended their crown in 2023, overcoming Mamelodi Sundowns on penalties after a goalless final. Goalkeeper Sipho Chaine proved to be the difference, producing three crucial saves in the shootout.

Orlando Pirates continued their dominance in 2024, defeating Stellenbosch FC 3-1 in the final to become the first club in the PSL era to win the MTN8 three seasons in succession.

The Buccaneers extended that remarkable record last season under Abdeslam Ouaddou. They defeated Stellenbosch FC 3-0 after extra time, with Tshepang Moremi scoring twice as Pirates secured their fourth consecutive crown and 14th MTN8 title overall.

The Citizens also know they can frustrate the Buccaneers. They held Orlando Pirates to a goalless Betway Premiership draw when the sides last met.

Victory on Saturday would take Orlando Pirates one step closer to an unprecedented fifth straight MTN8 crown, while Durban City will be targeting a major quarter-final upset at the Orlando Amstel Arena.

World.title: Pitso Mosimane named as new Bafana coach
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Pitso Mosimane is set for a return to the Bafana Bafana dugout.

The South African Football Association has approved his appointment as the new national team coach following the departure of Hugo Broos.

The decision was ratified at a Safa National Executive Committee meeting, with members backing Mosimane to take charge of the side that recently made history at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

South Africa reached the knockout rounds round for the first time, highlighted by a memorable victory over South Korea.

While SAFA said a few administrative details still need to be finalised, an official announcement is expected next week.

Mosimane was previously in charge of Bafana in a caretaker capacity in 2007 and from 2010 to 2012.

World.title: RFA flags enforcement gaps in freight sector
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Road Freight Association CEO Gavin Kelly said stronger enforcement is crucial to ease tensions over foreign driver employment in South Africa’s freight sector.

With truck driver associations threatening a freight shutdown, Kelly argued the issue begins with how companies are registered and monitored.

“We are not taking the right steps when we initially register companies. When we register companies, do we ask those companies who are their employees, before we allow the company to be registered?

“We need to ask questions like are you registered with the council that is applicable to your sector of business so that we have inspectors going to all the companies that are active in that sector.

“What happens now is that inspectors to companies they are aware of and that’s the real reason we have been struggling with this. Secondly, the deterrent has to meet this problem. It doesn’t help if you get rid of these foreign nationals and they reappear or the company just employs other foreigners because that destroys the operation of the sector in totality," Kelly said.

World.title: Coalition decisions will be crucial - Mnguni
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The race is on for political parties to garner votes ahead of the November local government elections.

But the reality is many municipalities may end up with coalition governments.

Rise Mzansi said fixing Johannesburg starts with principled leadership, transparent coalition agreements and no deals with parties tainted by criminality.

City of Johannesburg mayoral candidate Lukhona Mnguni said they work based on principles and coalition agreements ought to be signed.

“I do think that people are exceedingly disappointed in how the ANC is governing this city.

The ANC will probably have a huge task to justify why it must be included in a coalition. But those are conversations that become more material when you see the actual results.

“But I think starting with principles, quality of leadership, coalition agreements, and ensuring that residents have a much more transparent path to coalition formation than we have had previously,” Mnguni said.

World.title: Recovering Marchand to skip medleys at European swim champs
World.content:
PARIS - Swimming star Leon Marchand has cut back on the events he will compete in at the European championships starting Monday because of a lingering thigh injury.

The French federation confirmed Saturday that Marchand will not compete in the 200m and 400m individual medley events in Paris.

The Frenchman had already ruled out the 200m breaststroke but remains entered in the 200m butterfly and 400m freestyle that place less strain on the adductor muscles.

He may also participate in one or two relays with the French team.

"The injury is healing well, and recovery is largely complete. However, since competing in the 200m and 400m individual medley carries a non-negligible risk of recurrence, and to safeguard the remainder of the competition, the decision was made not to enter these races," explained team doctor Sebastien Le Garrec.

The four-time Olympic champion injured his adductor during the 200m breaststroke heats at the French championships in June, subsequently withdrawing from the rest of the competition.

He suffered a setback during a training session in Marseille three weeks later.

Earlier this month, he had confirmed his participation in the European championships, though he was doubtful regarding the 400m individual medley.

Ultimately, he decided to withdraw from the shorter distance as well as a precautionary measure.

The withdrawal from his two signature events is a major setback for the 24-year-old, who had made these championships the primary goal of his season.
